bsb.2:36: There was also a prophetess named Anna, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher, who was well along in years. She had been married for seven years,
bsb.2:37: and then was a widow to the age of eighty-four. She never left the temple, but worshiped night and day, fasting and praying.
bsb.2:38: Coming forward at that moment, she gave thanks to God and spoke about the Child to all who were waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem.
bsb.2:39: When Jesus’ parents had done everything required by the Law of the Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth.
bsb.2:40: And the Child grew and became strong. He was filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon Him.
bsb.2:41: Every year His parents went to Jerusalem for the Feast of the Passover.
bsb.2:42: And when He was twelve years old, they went up according to the custom of the Feast.
bsb.2:43: When those days were over and they were returning home, the boy Jesus remained behind in Jerusalem, but His parents were unaware He had stayed.
bsb.2:44: Assuming He was in their company, they traveled on for a day before they began to look for Him among their relatives and friends.
bsb.2:45: When they could not find Him, they returned to Jerusalem to search for Him.
bsb.2:46: Finally, after three days they found Him in the temple courts, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.
bsb.2:47: And all who heard Him were astounded at His understanding and His answers.
bsb.2:48: When His parents saw Him, they were astonished. “Child, why have You done this to us?” His mother asked. “Your father and I have been anxiously searching for You.”
bsb.2:49: “Why were you looking for Me?” He asked. “Did you not know that I had to be in My Father’s house?”
bsb.2:50: But they did not understand the statement He was making to them.
bsb.2:51: Then He went down to Nazareth with them and was obedient to them. But His mother treasured up all these things in her heart.
bsb.2:52: And Jesus grew in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and man.
bsb.3:1: In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, while Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea, Herod tetrarch of Galilee, his brother Philip tetrarch of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene,
bsb.3:2: during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John son of Zechariah in the wilderness.
bsb.3:3: He went into all the region around the Jordan, preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins,
bsb.3:4: as it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet: “A voice of one calling in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him.
bsb.3:5: Every valley shall be filled in, and every mountain and hill made low. The crooked ways shall be made straight, and the rough ways smooth.
bsb.3:6: And all humanity will see God’s salvation.’”
bsb.3:7: Then John said to the crowds coming out to be baptized by him, “You brood of vipers, who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?
bsb.3:8: Produce fruit, then, in keeping with repentance. And do not begin to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ For I tell you that out of these stones God can raise up children for Abraham.
bsb.3:9: The axe lies ready at the root of the trees, and every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.”
bsb.3:10: The crowds asked him, “What then should we do?”
bsb.3:11: John replied, “Whoever has two tunics should share with him who has none, and whoever has food should do the same.”
bsb.3:12: Even tax collectors came to be baptized. “Teacher,” they asked, “what should we do?”
bsb.3:13: “Collect no more than you are authorized,” he answered.
bsb.3:14: Then some soldiers asked him, “And what should we do?” “Do not take money by force or false accusation,” he said. “Be content with your wages.”
bsb.3:15: The people were waiting expectantly and were all wondering in their hearts if John could be the Christ.
bsb.3:16: John answered all of them: “I baptize you with water, but One more powerful than I will come, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.
bsb.3:17: His winnowing fork is in His hand to clear His threshing floor and to gather the wheat into His barn; but He will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.”
bsb.3:18: With these and many other exhortations, John proclaimed the good news to the people.
bsb.3:19: But when he rebuked Herod the tetrarch regarding his brother’s wife Herodias and all the evils he had done,
bsb.3:20: Herod added this to them all: He locked John up in prison.
bsb.3:21: When all the people were being baptized, Jesus was baptized too. And as He was praying, heaven was opened,
bsb.3:22: and the Holy Spirit descended on Him in a bodily form like a dove. And a voice came from heaven: “You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased.”
bsb.3:23: Jesus Himself was about thirty years old when He began His ministry. He was regarded as the son of Joseph, the son of Heli,
bsb.3:24: the son of Matthat, the son of Levi, the son of Melchi, the son of Jannai, the son of Joseph,
bsb.3:25: the son of Mattathias, the son of Amos, the son of Nahum, the son of Esli, the son of Naggai,
bsb.3:26: the son of Maath, the son of Mattathias, the son of Semein, the son of Josech, the son of Joda,
bsb.3:27: the son of Joanan, the son of Rhesa, the son of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, the son of Neri,
bsb.3:28: the son of Melchi, the son of Addi, the son of Cosam, the son of Elmadam, the son of Er,
bsb.3:29: the son of Joshua, the son of Eliezer, the son of Jorim, the son of Matthat, the son of Levi,
bsb.3:30: the son of Simeon, the son of Judah, the son of Joseph, the son of Jonam, the son of Eliakim,
bsb.3:31: the son of Melea, the son of Menna, the son of Mattatha, the son of Nathan, the son of David,
bsb.3:32: the son of Jesse, the son of Obed, the son of Boaz, the son of Sala, the son of Nahshon,
bsb.3:33: the son of Amminadab, the son of Admin, the son of Arni, the son of Hezron, the son of Perez, the son of Judah,
bsb.3:34: the son of Jacob, the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham, the son of Terah, the son of Nahor,
bsb.3:35: the son of Serug, the son of Reu, the son of Peleg, the son of Eber, the son of Shelah,
bsb.3:36: the son of Cainan, the son of Arphaxad, the son of Shem, the son of Noah, the son of Lamech,
bsb.3:37: the son of Methuselah, the son of Enoch, the son of Jared, the son of Mahalalel, the son of Cainan,
bsb.3:38: the son of Enosh, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, the son of God.
bsb.4:1: Then Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness,
bsb.4:2: where for forty days He was tempted by the devil. He ate nothing during those days, and when they had ended, He was hungry.
bsb.4:3: The devil said to Him, “If You are the Son of God, tell this stone to become bread.”
bsb.4:4: But Jesus answered, “It is written: ‘Man shall not live on bread alone.’”
bsb.4:5: Then the devil led Him up to a high place and showed Him in an instant all the kingdoms of the world.
bsb.4:6: “I will give You authority over all these kingdoms and all their glory,” he said. “For it has been relinquished to me, and I can give it to anyone I wish.
bsb.4:7: So if You worship me, it will all be Yours.”
bsb.4:8: But Jesus answered, “It is written: ‘Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only.’”
bsb.4:9: Then the devil led Him to Jerusalem and set Him on the pinnacle of the temple. “If You are the Son of God,” he said, “throw Yourself down from here.
bsb.4:10: For it is written: ‘He will command His angels concerning You to guard You carefully;
bsb.4:11: and they will lift You up in their hands, so that You will not strike Your foot against a stone.’”
bsb.4:12: But Jesus answered, “It also says, ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’”
bsb.4:13: When the devil had finished every temptation, he left Him until an opportune time.
bsb.4:14: Jesus returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit, and the news about Him spread throughout the surrounding region.
bsb.4:15: He taught in their synagogues and was glorified by everyone.
bsb.4:16: Then Jesus came to Nazareth, where He had been brought up. As was His custom, He entered the synagogue on the Sabbath. And when He stood up to read,
bsb.4:17: the scroll of the prophet Isaiah was handed to Him. Unrolling it, He found the place where it was written:
bsb.4:18: “The Spirit of the Lord is on Me, because He has anointed Me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent Me to proclaim liberty to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to release the oppressed,
bsb.4:19: to proclaim the year of the Lord’s favor.”
bsb.4:20: Then He rolled up the scroll, returned it to the attendant, and sat down. The eyes of everyone in the synagogue were fixed on Him,
bsb.4:21: and He began by saying, “Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your hearing.”
bsb.4:22: All spoke well of Him and marveled at the gracious words that came from His lips. “Isn’t this the son of Joseph?” they asked.
bsb.4:23: Jesus said to them, “Surely you will quote this proverb to Me: ‘Physician, heal yourself! Do here in Your hometown what we have heard that You did in Capernaum.’”
bsb.4:24: Then He added, “Truly I tell you, no prophet is accepted in his hometown.
bsb.4:25: But I tell you truthfully that there were many widows in Israel in the time of Elijah, when the sky was shut for three and a half years and great famine swept over all the land.
bsb.4:26: Yet Elijah was not sent to any of them, but to the widow of Zarephath in Sidon.
bsb.4:27: And there were many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet. Yet not one of them was cleansed—only Naaman the Syrian.”
bsb.4:28: On hearing this, all the people in the synagogue were enraged.
bsb.4:29: They got up, drove Him out of the town, and led Him to the brow of the hill on which the town was built, in order to throw Him over the cliff.
bsb.4:30: But Jesus passed through the crowd and went on His way.
bsb.4:31: Then He went down to Capernaum, a town in Galilee, and on the Sabbath He began to teach the people.
bsb.4:32: They were astonished at His teaching, because His message had authority.
bsb.4:33: In the synagogue there was a man possessed by the spirit of an unclean demon. He cried out in a loud voice,
bsb.4:34: “Ha! What do You want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have You come to destroy us? I know who You are—the Holy One of God!”
bsb.4:35: But Jesus rebuked the demon. “Be silent!” He said. “Come out of him!” At this, the demon threw the man down before them all and came out without harming him.
bsb.4:36: All the people were overcome with amazement and asked one another, “What is this message? With authority and power He commands the unclean spirits, and they come out!”
bsb.4:37: And the news about Jesus spread throughout the surrounding region.
bsb.4:38: After Jesus had left the synagogue, He went to the home of Simon, whose mother-in-law was suffering from a high fever. So they appealed to Jesus on her behalf,
bsb.4:39: and He stood over her and rebuked the fever, and it left her. And she got up at once and began to serve them.
bsb.4:40: At sunset, all who were ill with various diseases were brought to Jesus, and laying His hands on each one, He healed them.
bsb.4:41: Demons also came out of many people, shouting, “You are the Son of God!” But He rebuked the demons and would not allow them to speak, because they knew He was the Christ.
bsb.4:42: At daybreak, Jesus went out to a solitary place, and the crowds were looking for Him. They came to Him and tried to keep Him from leaving.
bsb.4:43: But Jesus told them, “I must preach the good news of the kingdom of God to the other towns as well, because that is why I was sent.”
bsb.4:44: And He continued to preach in the synagogues of Judea.
bsb.5:1: On one occasion, while Jesus was standing by the Lake of Gennesaret with the crowd pressing in on Him to hear the word of God,
bsb.5:2: He saw two boats at the edge of the lake. The fishermen had left them and were washing their nets.
bsb.5:3: Jesus got into the boat belonging to Simon and asked him to put out a little from shore. And sitting down, He taught the people from the boat.
bsb.5:4: When Jesus had finished speaking, He said to Simon, “Put out into deep water and let down your nets for a catch.”
bsb.5:5: “Master,” Simon replied, “we have worked hard all night without catching anything. But because You say so, I will let down the nets.”
bsb.5:6: When they had done so, they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to tear.
bsb.5:7: So they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them, and they came and filled both boats so full that they began to sink.
bsb.5:8: When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus’ knees. “Go away from me, Lord,” he said, “for I am a sinful man.”
bsb.5:9: For he and his companions were astonished at the catch of fish they had taken,
bsb.5:10: and so were his partners James and John, the sons of Zebedee. “Do not be afraid,” Jesus said to Simon. “From now on you will catch men.”
bsb.5:11: And when they had brought their boats ashore, they left everything and followed Him.
bsb.5:12: While Jesus was in one of the towns, a man came along who was covered with leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell facedown and begged Him, “Lord, if You are willing, You can make me clean.”
bsb.5:13: Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man. “I am willing,” He said. “Be clean!” And immediately the leprosy left him.
bsb.5:14: “Do not tell anyone,” Jesus instructed him. “But go, show yourself to the priest and present the offering Moses prescribed for your cleansing, as a testimony to them.”
bsb.5:15: But the news about Jesus spread all the more, and great crowds came to hear Him and to be healed of their sicknesses.
bsb.5:16: Yet He frequently withdrew to the wilderness to pray.
bsb.5:17: One day Jesus was teaching, and the Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there. People had come from Jerusalem and from every village of Galilee and Judea, and the power of the Lord was present for Him to heal the sick.
bsb.5:18: Just then some men came carrying a paralyzed man on a mat. They tried to bring him inside to set him before Jesus,
bsb.5:19: but they could not find a way through the crowd. So they went up on the roof and lowered him on his mat through the tiles into the middle of the crowd, right in front of Jesus.
bsb.5:20: When Jesus saw their faith, He said, “Friend, your sins are forgiven.”
bsb.5:21: But the scribes and Pharisees began thinking to themselves, “Who is this man who speaks blasphemy? Who can forgive sins but God alone?”
bsb.5:22: Knowing what they were thinking, Jesus replied, “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?
bsb.5:23: Which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk?’
bsb.5:24: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on the earth to forgive sins...” He said to the paralytic, “I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
bsb.5:25: And immediately the man stood up before them, took what he had been lying on, and went home glorifying God.
bsb.5:26: Everyone was taken with amazement and glorified God. They were filled with awe and said, “We have seen remarkable things today.”
bsb.5:27: After this, Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth. “Follow Me,” He told him,
bsb.5:28: and Levi got up, left everything, and followed Him.
bsb.5:29: Then Levi hosted a great banquet for Jesus at his house. A large crowd of tax collectors was there, along with others who were eating with them.
bsb.5:30: But the Pharisees and their scribes complained to Jesus’ disciples, “Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”
bsb.5:31: Jesus answered, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.
bsb.5:32: I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance.”
bsb.5:33: Then they said to Him, “John’s disciples and those of the Pharisees frequently fast and pray, but Yours keep on eating and drinking.”
bsb.5:34: Jesus replied, “Can you make the guests of the bridegroom fast while He is with them?
bsb.5:35: But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.”
bsb.5:36: He also told them a parable: “No one tears a piece of cloth from a new garment and sews it on an old one. If he does, he will tear the new garment as well, and the patch from the new will not match the old.
bsb.5:37: And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the new wine will burst the skins, the wine will spill, and the wineskins will be ruined.
bsb.5:38: Instead, new wine is poured into new wineskins.
bsb.5:39: And no one after drinking old wine wants new, for he says, ‘The old is better.’”
bsb.6:1: One Sabbath Jesus was passing through the grainfields, and His disciples began to pick the heads of grain, rub them in their hands, and eat them.
bsb.6:2: But some of the Pharisees asked, “Why are you doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath?”
bsb.6:3: Jesus replied, “Have you not read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?
bsb.6:4: He entered the house of God, took the consecrated bread and gave it to his companions, and ate what is lawful only for the priests to eat.”
bsb.6:5: Then Jesus declared, “The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
bsb.6:6: On another Sabbath Jesus entered the synagogue and was teaching, and a man was there whose right hand was withered.
bsb.6:7: Looking for a reason to accuse Jesus, the scribes and Pharisees were watching Him closely to see if He would heal on the Sabbath.
bsb.6:8: But Jesus knew their thoughts and said to the man with the withered hand, “Get up and stand among us.” So he got up and stood there.
bsb.6:9: Then Jesus said to them, “I ask you, which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?”
bsb.6:10: And after looking around at all of them, He said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He did so, and it was restored.
bsb.6:11: But the scribes and Pharisees were filled with rage and began to discuss with one another what they might do to Jesus.
bsb.6:12: In those days Jesus went out to the mountain to pray, and He spent the night in prayer to God.
bsb.6:13: When daylight came, He called His disciples to Him and chose twelve of them, whom He also designated as apostles:
bsb.6:14: Simon, whom He named Peter, and his brother Andrew; James and John; Philip and Bartholomew;
bsb.6:15: Matthew and Thomas; James son of Alphaeus and Simon called the Zealot;
bsb.6:16: Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.
bsb.6:17: Then Jesus came down with them and stood on a level place. A large crowd of His disciples was there, along with a great number of people from all over Judea, Jerusalem, and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon.
bsb.6:18: They had come to hear Him and to be healed of their diseases, and those troubled by unclean spirits were healed.
bsb.6:19: The entire crowd was trying to touch Him, because power was coming from Him and healing them all.
bsb.6:20: Looking up at His disciples, Jesus said: “Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.
bsb.6:21: Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
bsb.6:22: Blessed are you when people hate you, and when they exclude you and insult you and reject your name as evil because of the Son of Man.
bsb.6:23: Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, because great is your reward in heaven. For their fathers treated the prophets in the same way.
bsb.6:24: But woe to you who are rich, for you have already received your comfort.
bsb.6:25: Woe to you who are well fed now, for you will hunger. Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.
bsb.6:26: Woe to you when all men speak well of you, for their fathers treated the false prophets in the same way.
bsb.6:27: But to those of you who will listen, I say: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,
bsb.6:28: bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you.
bsb.6:29: If someone strikes you on one cheek, turn to him the other also. And if someone takes your cloak, do not withhold your tunic as well.
bsb.6:30: Give to everyone who asks you, and if anyone takes what is yours, do not demand it back.
bsb.6:31: Do to others as you would have them do to you.
bsb.6:32: If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners love those who love them.
bsb.6:33: If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners do the same.
bsb.6:34: And if you lend to those from whom you expect repayment, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, expecting to be repaid in full.
bsb.6:35: But love your enemies, do good to them, and lend to them, expecting nothing in return. Then your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High; for He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked.
bsb.6:36: Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
bsb.6:37: Do not judge, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.
bsb.6:38: Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over will be poured into your lap. For with the measure you use, it will be measured back to you.”
bsb.6:39: Jesus also told them a parable: “Can a blind man lead a blind man? Will they not both fall into a pit?
bsb.6:40: A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like his teacher.
bsb.6:41: Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye, but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?
bsb.6:42: How can you say, ‘Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye,’ while you yourself fail to see the beam in your own eye? You hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.
bsb.6:43: No good tree bears bad fruit, nor does a bad tree bear good fruit.
bsb.6:44: For each tree is known by its own fruit. Indeed, figs are not gathered from thornbushes, nor grapes from brambles.
bsb.6:45: The good man brings good things out of the good treasure of his heart, and the evil man brings evil things out of the evil treasure of his heart. For out of the overflow of the heart, the mouth speaks.
bsb.6:46: Why do you call Me ‘Lord, Lord,’ but not do what I say?
bsb.6:47: I will show you what he is like who comes to Me and hears My words and acts on them:
bsb.6:48: He is like a man building a house, who dug down deep and laid his foundation on the rock. When the flood came, the torrent crashed against that house but could not shake it, because it was well built.
bsb.6:49: But the one who hears My words and does not act on them is like a man who built his house on ground without a foundation. The torrent crashed against that house, and immediately it fell—and great was its destruction!”
bsb.7:1: When Jesus had concluded His discourse in the hearing of the people, He went to Capernaum.
bsb.7:2: There a highly valued servant of a centurion was sick and about to die.
bsb.7:3: When the centurion heard about Jesus, he sent some Jewish elders to ask Him to come and heal his servant.
bsb.7:4: They came to Jesus and pleaded with Him earnestly, “This man is worthy to have You grant this,
bsb.7:5: for he loves our nation and has built our synagogue.”
bsb.7:6: So Jesus went with them. But when He was not far from the house, the centurion sent friends with the message: “Lord, do not trouble Yourself, for I am not worthy to have You come under my roof.
bsb.7:7: That is why I did not consider myself worthy to come to You. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
bsb.7:8: For I myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell one to go, and he goes; and another to come, and he comes. I tell my servant to do something, and he does it.”
bsb.7:9: When Jesus heard this, He marveled at the centurion. Turning to the crowd following Him, He said, “I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such great faith.”
bsb.7:10: And when the messengers returned to the house, they found the servant in good health.
bsb.7:11: Soon afterward, Jesus went to a town called Nain. His disciples went with Him, accompanied by a large crowd.
bsb.7:12: As He approached the town gate, He saw a dead man being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow. And a large crowd from the town was with her.
bsb.7:13: When the Lord saw her, He had compassion on her and said, “Do not weep.”
bsb.7:14: Then He went up and touched the coffin, and those carrying it stood still. “Young man,” He said, “I tell you, get up!”
bsb.7:15: And the dead man sat up and began to speak! Then Jesus gave him back to his mother.
bsb.7:16: A sense of awe swept over all of them, and they glorified God. “A great prophet has appeared among us!” they said. “God has visited His people!”
bsb.7:17: And the news about Jesus spread throughout Judea and all the surrounding region.
bsb.7:18: Then John’s disciples informed him about all these things.
bsb.7:19: So John called two of his disciples and sent them to ask the Lord, “Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?”
bsb.7:20: When the men came to Jesus, they said, “John the Baptist sent us to ask, ‘Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?’”
bsb.7:21: At that very hour Jesus healed many people of their diseases, afflictions, and evil spirits, and He gave sight to many who were blind.
bsb.7:22: So He replied, “Go back and report to John what you have seen and heard: The blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is preached to the poor.
bsb.7:23: Blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of Me.”
bsb.7:24: After John’s messengers had left, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed swaying in the wind?
bsb.7:25: Otherwise, what did you go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? Look, those who wear elegant clothing and live in luxury are found in palaces.
bsb.7:26: What then did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
bsb.7:27: This is the one about whom it is written: ‘Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You.’
bsb.7:28: I tell you, among those born of women there is no one greater than John, yet even the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.”
bsb.7:29: All the people who heard this, even the tax collectors, acknowledged God’s justice. For they had received the baptism of John.
bsb.7:30: But the Pharisees and experts in the law rejected God’s purpose for themselves, because they had not been baptized by John.
bsb.7:31: “To what, then, can I compare the men of this generation? What are they like?
bsb.7:32: They are like children sitting in the marketplace and calling out to one another: ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not weep.’
bsb.7:33: For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon!’
bsb.7:34: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’
bsb.7:35: But wisdom is vindicated by all her children.”
bsb.7:36: Then one of the Pharisees invited Jesus to eat with him, and He entered the Pharisee’s house and reclined at the table.
bsb.7:37: When a sinful woman from that town learned that Jesus was dining there, she brought an alabaster jar of perfume.
bsb.7:38: As she stood behind Him at His feet weeping, she began to wet His feet with her tears and wipe them with her hair. Then she kissed His feet and anointed them with the perfume.
bsb.7:39: When the Pharisee who had invited Jesus saw this, he said to himself, “If this man were a prophet, He would know who this is and what kind of woman is touching Him—for she is a sinner!”
bsb.7:40: But Jesus answered him, “Simon, I have something to tell you.” “Tell me, Teacher,” he said.
bsb.7:41: “Two men were debtors to a certain moneylender. One owed him five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
bsb.7:42: When they were unable to repay him, he forgave both of them. Which one, then, will love him more?”
bsb.7:43: “I suppose the one who was forgiven more,” Simon replied. “You have judged correctly,” Jesus said.
bsb.7:44: And turning toward the woman, He said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? When I entered your house, you did not give Me water for My feet, but she wet My feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.
bsb.7:45: You did not greet Me with a kiss, but she has not stopped kissing My feet since I arrived.
bsb.7:46: You did not anoint My head with oil, but she has anointed My feet with perfume.
bsb.7:47: Therefore I tell you, because her many sins have been forgiven, she has loved much. But he who has been forgiven little loves little.”
bsb.7:48: Then Jesus said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”
bsb.7:49: But those at the table began to say to themselves, “Who is this who even forgives sins?”
bsb.7:50: And Jesus told the woman, “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”
bsb.8:1: Soon afterward, Jesus traveled from one town and village to another, preaching and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God. The Twelve were with Him,
bsb.8:2: as well as some women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities: Mary called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out,
bsb.8:3: Joanna the wife of Herod’s household manager Chuza, Susanna, and many others. These women were ministering to them out of their own means.
bsb.8:4: While a large crowd was gathering and people were coming to Jesus from town after town, He told them this parable:
bsb.8:5: “A farmer went out to sow his seed. And as he was sowing, some seed fell along the path, where it was trampled, and the birds of the air devoured it.
bsb.8:6: Some fell on rocky ground, and when it came up, the seedlings withered because they had no moisture.
bsb.8:7: Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up with it and choked the seedlings.
bsb.8:8: Still other seed fell on good soil, where it sprang up and produced a crop—a hundredfold.” As Jesus said this, He called out, “He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”
bsb.8:9: Then His disciples asked Him what this parable meant.
bsb.8:10: He replied, “The knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of God has been given to you, but to others I speak in parables, so that, ‘though seeing, they may not see; though hearing, they may not understand.’
bsb.8:11: Now this is the meaning of the parable: The seed is the word of God.
bsb.8:12: The seeds along the path are those who hear, but the devil comes and takes away the word from their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved.
bsb.8:13: The seeds on rocky ground are those who hear the word and receive it with joy, but they have no root. They believe for a season, but in the time of testing, they fall away.
bsb.8:14: The seeds that fell among the thorns are those who hear, but as they go on their way, they are choked by the worries, riches, and pleasures of this life, and their fruit does not mature.
bsb.8:15: But the seeds on good soil are those with a noble and good heart, who hear the word, cling to it, and by persevering produce a crop.
bsb.8:16: No one lights a lamp and covers it with a jar or puts it under a bed. Instead, he sets it on a stand, so those who enter can see the light.
bsb.8:17: For there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed, and nothing concealed that will not be made known and brought to light.
bsb.8:18: Pay attention, therefore, to how you listen. Whoever has will be given more, but whoever does not have, even what he thinks he has will be taken away from him.”
bsb.8:19: Then Jesus’ mother and brothers came to see Him, but they were unable to reach Him because of the crowd.
bsb.8:20: He was told, “Your mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to see You.”
bsb.8:21: But He replied, “My mother and brothers are those who hear the word of God and carry it out.”
bsb.8:22: One day Jesus said to His disciples, “Let us cross to the other side of the lake.” So He got into a boat with them and set out.
bsb.8:23: As they sailed, He fell asleep, and a windstorm came down on the lake, so that the boat was being swamped, and they were in great danger.
bsb.8:24: The disciples went and woke Him, saying, “Master, Master, we are perishing!” Then Jesus got up and rebuked the wind and the raging waters, and they subsided, and all was calm.
bsb.8:25: “Where is your faith?” He asked. Frightened and amazed, they asked one another, “Who is this? He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey Him!”
bsb.8:26: Then they sailed to the region of the Gerasenes, across the lake from Galilee.
bsb.8:27: When Jesus stepped ashore, He was met by a demon-possessed man from the town. For a long time this man had not worn clothing or lived in a house, but he stayed in the tombs.
bsb.8:28: When the man saw Jesus, he cried out and fell down before Him, shouting in a loud voice, “What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg You not to torture me!”
bsb.8:29: For Jesus had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. Many times it had seized him, and though he was bound with chains and shackles, he had broken the chains and been driven by the demon into solitary places.
bsb.8:30: “What is your name?” Jesus asked. “Legion,” he replied, because many demons had gone into him.
bsb.8:31: And the demons kept begging Jesus not to order them to go into the Abyss.
bsb.8:32: There on the hillside a large herd of pigs was feeding. So the demons begged Jesus to let them enter the pigs, and He gave them permission.
bsb.8:33: Then the demons came out of the man and went into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and was drowned.
bsb.8:34: When those tending the pigs saw what had happened, they ran off and reported this in the town and countryside.
bsb.8:35: So the people went out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus and found the man whom the demons had left, sitting at Jesus’ feet, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.
bsb.8:36: Meanwhile, those who had seen it reported how the demon-possessed man had been healed.
bsb.8:37: Then all the people of the region of the Gerasenes asked Jesus to depart from them, because great fear had taken hold of them. So He got into the boat and started back.
bsb.8:38: The man whom the demons had left begged to go with Jesus. But He sent him away, saying,
bsb.8:39: “Return home and describe how much God has done for you.” So the man went away and proclaimed all over the town how much Jesus had done for him.
bsb.8:40: When Jesus returned, the crowd welcomed Him, for they had all been waiting for Him.
bsb.8:41: Just then a synagogue leader named Jairus came and fell at Jesus’ feet. He begged Him to come to his house,
bsb.8:42: because his only daughter, who was about twelve, was dying. As Jesus went with him, the crowds pressed around Him,
bsb.8:43: including a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years. She had spent all her money on physicians, but no one was able to heal her.
bsb.8:44: She came up behind Jesus and touched the fringe of His cloak, and immediately her bleeding stopped.
bsb.8:45: “Who touched Me?” Jesus asked. But they all denied it. “Master,” said Peter, “the people are crowding and pressing against You.”
bsb.8:46: But Jesus declared, “Someone touched Me, for I know that power has gone out from Me.”
bsb.8:47: Then the woman, seeing that she could not escape notice, came trembling and fell down before Him. In the presence of all the people, she explained why she had touched Him and how she had immediately been healed.
bsb.8:48: “Daughter,” said Jesus, “your faith has healed you. Go in peace.”
bsb.8:49: While He was still speaking, someone arrived from the house of the synagogue leader. “Your daughter is dead,” he told Jairus. “Do not bother the Teacher anymore.”
bsb.8:50: But Jesus overheard them and said to Jairus, “Do not be afraid; just believe, and she will be healed.”
bsb.8:51: When He entered the house, He did not allow anyone to go in with Him except Peter, John, James, and the child’s father and mother.
bsb.8:52: Meanwhile, everyone was weeping and mourning for her. But Jesus said, “Stop weeping; she is not dead but asleep.”
bsb.8:53: And they laughed at Him, knowing that she was dead.
bsb.8:54: But Jesus took her by the hand and called out, “Child, get up!”
bsb.8:55: Her spirit returned, and at once she got up. And He directed that she be given something to eat.
bsb.8:56: Her parents were astounded, but Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone what had happened.
bsb.9:1: Then Jesus called the Twelve together and gave them power and authority over all demons, and power to cure diseases.
bsb.9:2: And He sent them out to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.
bsb.9:3: “Take nothing for the journey,” He told them, “no staff, no bag, no bread, no money, no second tunic.
bsb.9:4: Whatever house you enter, stay there until you leave that area.
bsb.9:5: If anyone does not welcome you, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that town, as a testimony against them.”
bsb.9:6: So they set out and went from village to village, preaching the gospel and healing people everywhere.
bsb.9:7: When Herod the tetrarch heard about all that was happening, he was perplexed. For some were saying that John had risen from the dead,
bsb.9:8: others that Elijah had appeared, and still others that a prophet of old had arisen.
bsb.9:9: “I beheaded John,” Herod said, “but who is this man I hear such things about?” And he kept trying to see Jesus.
bsb.9:10: Then the apostles returned and reported to Jesus all that they had done. Taking them away privately, He withdrew to a town called Bethsaida.
bsb.9:11: But the crowds found out and followed Him. He welcomed them and spoke to them about the kingdom of God, and He healed those who needed healing.
bsb.9:12: As the day neared its end, the Twelve came to Jesus and said, “Dismiss the crowd so they can go to the surrounding villages and countryside for lodging and provisions. For we are in a desolate place here.”
bsb.9:13: But Jesus told them, “You give them something to eat.” “We have only five loaves of bread and two fish,” they answered, “unless we go and buy food for all these people.”
bsb.9:14: (There were about five thousand men.) He told His disciples, “Have them sit down in groups of about fifty each.”
bsb.9:15: They did so, and everyone was seated.
bsb.9:16: Taking the five loaves and the two fish and looking up to heaven, Jesus spoke a blessing and broke them. Then He gave them to the disciples to set before the people.
bsb.9:17: They all ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.
bsb.9:18: One day as Jesus was praying in private and the disciples were with Him, He questioned them: “Who do the crowds say I am?”
bsb.9:19: They replied, “Some say John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and still others, that a prophet of old has arisen.”
bsb.9:20: “But what about you?” Jesus asked. “Who do you say I am?” Peter answered, “The Christ of God.”
bsb.9:21: Jesus strictly warned them not to tell this to anyone.
bsb.9:22: “The Son of Man must suffer many things,” He said. “He must be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and He must be killed and on the third day be raised to life.”
bsb.9:23: Then Jesus said to all of them, “If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow Me.
bsb.9:24: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake will save it.
bsb.9:25: What does it profit a man to gain the whole world, yet lose or forfeit his very self?
bsb.9:26: If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of him when He comes in His glory and in the glory of the Father and of the holy angels.
bsb.9:27: But I tell you truthfully, some who are standing here will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God.”
bsb.9:28: About eight days after Jesus had said these things, He took with Him Peter, John, and James, and went up on a mountain to pray.
bsb.9:29: And as He was praying, the appearance of His face changed, and His clothes became radiantly white.
bsb.9:30: Suddenly two men, Moses and Elijah, began talking with Jesus.
bsb.9:31: They appeared in glory and spoke about His departure, which He was about to accomplish at Jerusalem.
bsb.9:32: Meanwhile Peter and his companions were overcome by sleep, but when they awoke, they saw Jesus’ glory and the two men standing with Him.
bsb.9:33: As Moses and Elijah were leaving, Peter said to Jesus, “Master, it is good for us to be here. Let us put up three shelters—one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” (He did not know what he was saying.)
bsb.9:34: While Peter was speaking, a cloud appeared and enveloped them, and they were afraid as they entered the cloud.
bsb.9:35: And a voice came from the cloud, saying, “This is My Son, whom I have chosen. Listen to Him!”
bsb.9:36: After the voice had spoken, only Jesus was present with them. The disciples kept this to themselves, and in those days they did not tell anyone what they had seen.
bsb.9:37: The next day, when they came down from the mountain, Jesus was met by a large crowd.
bsb.9:38: Suddenly a man in the crowd cried out, “Teacher, I beg You to look at my son, for he is my only child.
bsb.9:39: A spirit keeps seizing him, and he screams abruptly. It throws him into convulsions so that he foams at the mouth. It keeps mauling him and rarely departs from him.
bsb.9:40: I begged Your disciples to drive it out, but they were unable.”
bsb.9:41: “O unbelieving and perverse generation!” Jesus replied. “How long must I remain with you and put up with you? Bring your son here.”
bsb.9:42: Even while the boy was approaching, the demon slammed him to the ground in a convulsion. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.
bsb.9:43: And they were all astonished at the greatness of God. While everyone was marveling at all that Jesus was doing, He said to His disciples,
bsb.9:44: “Let these words sink into your ears: The Son of Man is about to be delivered into the hands of men.”
bsb.9:45: But they did not understand this statement. It was veiled from them so that they could not comprehend it, and they were afraid to ask Him about it.
bsb.9:46: Then an argument started among the disciples as to which of them would be the greatest.
bsb.9:47: But Jesus, knowing the thoughts of their hearts, had a little child stand beside Him.
bsb.9:48: And He said to them, “Whoever welcomes this little child in My name welcomes Me, and whoever welcomes Me welcomes the One who sent Me. For whoever is the least among all of you, he is the greatest.”
bsb.9:49: “Master,” said John, “we saw someone driving out demons in Your name, and we tried to stop him, because he does not accompany us.”
bsb.9:50: “Do not stop him,” Jesus replied, “for whoever is not against you is for you.”
bsb.9:51: As the day of His ascension approached, Jesus resolutely set out for Jerusalem.
bsb.9:52: He sent messengers on ahead, who went into a village of the Samaritans to make arrangements for Him.
bsb.9:53: But the people there refused to welcome Him, because He was heading for Jerusalem.
bsb.9:54: When the disciples James and John saw this, they asked, “Lord, do You want us to call down fire from heaven to consume them?”
bsb.9:55: But Jesus turned and rebuked them.
bsb.9:56: And He and His disciples went on to another village.
bsb.9:57: As they were walking along the road, someone said to Jesus, “I will follow You wherever You go.”
bsb.9:58: Jesus replied, “Foxes have dens and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.”
bsb.9:59: Then He said to another man, “Follow Me.” The man replied, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.”
bsb.9:60: But Jesus told him, “Let the dead bury their own dead. You, however, go and proclaim the kingdom of God.”
bsb.9:61: Still another said, “I will follow You, Lord; but first let me bid farewell to my family.”
bsb.9:62: Then Jesus declared, “No one who puts his hand to the plow and then looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.”
bsb.10:1: After this, the Lord appointed seventy-two others and sent them two by two ahead of Him to every town and place He was about to visit.
bsb.10:2: And He told them, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few. Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into His harvest.
bsb.10:3: Go! I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.
bsb.10:4: Carry no purse or bag or sandals. Do not greet anyone along the road.
bsb.10:5: Whatever house you enter, begin by saying, ‘Peace to this house.’
bsb.10:6: If a man of peace is there, your peace will rest on him; if not, it will return to you.
bsb.10:7: Stay at the same house, eating and drinking whatever you are offered. For the worker is worthy of his wages. Do not move around from house to house.
bsb.10:8: If you enter a town and they welcome you, eat whatever is set before you.
bsb.10:9: Heal the sick who are there and tell them, ‘The kingdom of God is near you.’
bsb.10:10: But if you enter a town and they do not welcome you, go into the streets and declare,
bsb.10:11: ‘Even the dust of your town that clings to our feet, we wipe off as a testimony against you. Yet be sure of this: The kingdom of God is near.’
bsb.10:12: I tell you, it will be more bearable on that day for Sodom than for that town.
bsb.10:13: Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
bsb.10:14: But it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for you.
bsb.10:15: And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? No, you will be brought down to Hades!
bsb.10:16: Whoever listens to you listens to Me; whoever rejects you rejects Me; and whoever rejects Me rejects the One who sent Me.”
bsb.10:17: The seventy-two returned with joy and said, “Lord, even the demons submit to us in Your name.”
bsb.10:18: So He told them, “I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven.
bsb.10:19: Behold, I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy. Nothing will harm you.
bsb.10:20: Nevertheless, do not rejoice that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.”
bsb.10:21: At that time Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and declared, “I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for this was well-pleasing in Your sight.
bsb.10:22: All things have been entrusted to Me by My Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, and no one knows who the Father is except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.”
bsb.10:23: Then Jesus turned to the disciples and said privately, “Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.
bsb.10:24: For I tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it.”
bsb.10:25: One day an expert in the law stood up to test Him. “Teacher,” he asked, “what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
bsb.10:26: “What is written in the Law?” Jesus replied. “How do you read it?”
bsb.10:27: He answered, “‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind’ and ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’”
bsb.10:28: “You have answered correctly,” Jesus said. “Do this and you will live.”
bsb.10:29: But wanting to justify himself, he asked Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?”
bsb.10:30: Jesus took up this question and said, “A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho when he fell into the hands of robbers. They stripped him, beat him, and went away, leaving him half dead.
bsb.10:31: Now by chance a priest was going down the same road, but when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.
bsb.10:32: So too, when a Levite came to that spot and saw him, he passed by on the other side.
bsb.10:33: But when a Samaritan on a journey came upon him, he looked at him and had compassion.
bsb.10:34: He went to him and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. Then he put him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
bsb.10:35: The next day he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper. ‘Take care of him,’ he said, ‘and on my return I will repay you for any additional expense.’
bsb.10:36: Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of robbers?”
bsb.10:37: “The one who showed him mercy,” replied the expert in the law. Then Jesus told him, “Go and do likewise.”
bsb.10:38: As they traveled along, Jesus entered a village where a woman named Martha welcomed Him into her home.
bsb.10:39: She had a sister named Mary, who sat at the Lord’s feet listening to His message.
bsb.10:40: But Martha was distracted by all the preparations to be made. She came to Jesus and said, “Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her to help me!”
bsb.10:41: “Martha, Martha,” the Lord replied, “you are worried and upset about many things.
bsb.10:42: But only one thing is necessary. Mary has chosen the good portion, and it will not be taken away from her.”
bsb.11:1: One day in a place where Jesus had just finished praying, one of His disciples requested, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John taught his disciples.”
bsb.11:2: So Jesus told them, “When you pray, say: ‘Father, hallowed be Your name. Your kingdom come.
bsb.11:3: Give us each day our daily bread.
bsb.11:4: And forgive us our sins, for we also forgive everyone who sins against us. And lead us not into temptation.’”
bsb.11:5: Then Jesus said to them, “Suppose one of you goes to his friend at midnight and says, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves of bread,
bsb.11:6: because a friend of mine has come to me on a journey, and I have nothing to set before him.’
bsb.11:7: And suppose the one inside answers, ‘Do not bother me. My door is already shut, and my children and I are in bed. I cannot get up to give you anything.’
bsb.11:8: I tell you, even though he will not get up to provide for him because of his friendship, yet because of the man’s persistence, he will get up and give him as much as he needs.
bsb.11:9: So I tell you: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.
bsb.11:10: For everyone who asks receives; he who seeks finds; and to him who knocks, the door will be opened.
bsb.11:11: What father among you, if his son asks for a fish, will give him a snake instead?
bsb.11:12: Or if he asks for an egg, will give him a scorpion?
bsb.11:13: So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him!”
bsb.11:14: One day Jesus was driving out a demon that was mute. And when the demon was gone, the man who had been mute spoke. The crowds were amazed,
bsb.11:15: but some of them said, “It is by Beelzebul, the prince of the demons, that He drives out demons.”
bsb.11:16: And others tested Him by demanding a sign from heaven.
bsb.11:17: Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste, and a house divided against a house will fall.
bsb.11:18: If Satan is divided against himself, how can his kingdom stand? After all, you say that I drive out demons by Beelzebul.
bsb.11:19: And if I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons drive them out? So then, they will be your judges.
bsb.11:20: But if I drive out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
bsb.11:21: When a strong man, fully armed, guards his house, his possessions are secure.
bsb.11:22: But when someone stronger attacks and overpowers him, he takes away the armor in which the man trusted, and then he divides up his plunder.
bsb.11:23: He who is not with Me is against Me, and he who does not gather with Me scatters.
bsb.11:24: When an unclean spirit comes out of a man, it passes through arid places seeking rest and does not find it. Then it says, ‘I will return to the house I left.’
bsb.11:25: On its return, it finds the house swept clean and put in order.
bsb.11:26: Then it goes and brings seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they go in and dwell there. And the final plight of that man is worse than the first.”
bsb.11:27: As Jesus was saying these things, a woman in the crowd raised her voice and said, “Blessed is the womb that bore You, and blessed are the breasts that nursed You!”
bsb.11:28: But He replied, “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it.”
bsb.11:29: As the crowds were increasing, Jesus said, “This is a wicked generation. It demands a sign, but none will be given it except the sign of Jonah.
bsb.11:30: For as Jonah was a sign to the Ninevites, so the Son of Man will be a sign to this generation.
bsb.11:31: The Queen of the South will rise at the judgment with the men of this generation and condemn them; for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and now One greater than Solomon is here.
bsb.11:32: The men of Nineveh will stand at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and now One greater than Jonah is here.
bsb.11:33: No one lights a lamp and puts it in a cellar or under a basket. Instead, he sets it on a stand, so those who enter can see the light.
bsb.11:34: Your eye is the lamp of your body. When your eyes are good, your whole body also is full of light. But when they are bad, your body is full of darkness.
bsb.11:35: Be careful, then, that the light within you is not darkness.
bsb.11:36: So if your whole body is full of light, with no part of it in darkness, you will be radiant, as though a lamp were shining on you.”
bsb.11:37: As Jesus was speaking, a Pharisee invited Him to dine with him; so He went in and reclined at the table.
bsb.11:38: But the Pharisee was surprised to see that Jesus did not first wash before the meal.
bsb.11:39: “Now then,” said the Lord, “you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside you are full of greed and wickedness.
bsb.11:40: You fools! Did not the One who made the outside make the inside as well?
bsb.11:41: But give as alms the things that are within you, and you will see that everything is clean for you.
bsb.11:42: Woe to you Pharisees! You pay tithes of mint, rue, and every herb, but you disregard justice and the love of God. You should have practiced the latter without neglecting the former.
bsb.11:43: Woe to you Pharisees! You love the chief seats in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces.
bsb.11:44: Woe to you! For you are like unmarked graves, which men walk over without even noticing.”
bsb.11:45: One of the experts in the law told Him, “Teacher, when You say these things, You insult us as well.”
bsb.11:46: “Woe to you as well, experts in the law!” He replied. “You weigh men down with heavy burdens, but you yourselves will not lift a finger to lighten their load.
bsb.11:47: Woe to you! You build tombs for the prophets, but it was your fathers who killed them.
bsb.11:48: So you are witnesses consenting to the deeds of your fathers: They killed the prophets, and you build their tombs.
bsb.11:49: Because of this, the wisdom of God said, ‘I will send them prophets and apostles; some of them they will kill and others they will persecute.’
bsb.11:50: As a result, this generation will be charged with the blood of all the prophets that has been shed since the foundation of the world,
bsb.11:51: from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who was killed between the altar and the sanctuary. Yes, I tell you, all of it will be charged to this generation.
bsb.11:52: Woe to you experts in the law! For you have taken away the key to knowledge. You yourselves have not entered, and you have hindered those who were entering.”
bsb.11:53: As Jesus went on from there, the scribes and Pharisees began to oppose Him bitterly and to ply Him with questions about many things,
bsb.11:54: waiting to catch Him in something He might say.
bsb.12:1: In the meantime, a crowd of many thousands had gathered, so that they were trampling one another. Jesus began to speak first to His disciples: “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
bsb.12:2: There is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.
bsb.12:3: What you have spoken in the dark will be heard in the daylight, and what you have whispered in the inner rooms will be proclaimed from the housetops.
bsb.12:4: I tell you, My friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that can do no more.
bsb.12:5: But I will show you whom you should fear: Fear the One who, after you have been killed, has authority to throw you into hell. Yes, I tell you, fear Him!
bsb.12:6: Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? Yet not one of them is forgotten by God.
bsb.12:7: And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
bsb.12:8: I tell you, everyone who confesses Me before men, the Son of Man will also confess him before the angels of God.
bsb.12:9: But whoever denies Me before men will be denied before the angels of God.
bsb.12:10: And everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
bsb.12:11: When you are brought before synagogues, rulers, and authorities, do not worry about how to defend yourselves or what to say.
bsb.12:12: For at that time the Holy Spirit will teach you what you should say.”
bsb.12:13: Someone in the crowd said to Him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”
bsb.12:14: But Jesus replied, “Man, who appointed Me judge or executor between you?”
bsb.12:15: And He said to them, “Watch out! Guard yourselves against every form of greed, for one’s life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.”
bsb.12:16: Then He told them a parable: “The ground of a certain rich man produced an abundance.
bsb.12:17: So he thought to himself, ‘What shall I do, since I have nowhere to store my crops?’
bsb.12:18: Then he said, ‘This is what I will do: I will tear down my barns and will build bigger ones, and there I will store up all my grain and my goods.
bsb.12:19: Then I will say to myself, “You have plenty of good things laid up for many years. Take it easy. Eat, drink, and be merry!”’
bsb.12:20: But God said to him, ‘You fool! This very night your life will be required of you. Then who will own what you have accumulated?’
bsb.12:21: This is how it will be for anyone who stores up treasure for himself but is not rich toward God.”
bsb.12:22: Then Jesus said to His disciples, “Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.
bsb.12:23: For life is more than food, and the body more than clothes.
bsb.12:24: Consider the ravens: They do not sow or reap, they have no storehouse or barn; yet God feeds them. How much more valuable you are than the birds!
bsb.12:25: Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?
bsb.12:26: So if you cannot do such a small thing, why do you worry about the rest?
bsb.12:27: Consider how the lilies grow: They do not labor or spin. Yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.
bsb.12:28: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, how much more will He clothe you, O you of little faith!
bsb.12:29: And do not be concerned about what you will eat or drink. Do not worry about it.
bsb.12:30: For the Gentiles of the world strive after all these things, and your Father knows that you need them.
bsb.12:31: But seek His kingdom, and these things will be added unto you.
bsb.12:32: Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.
bsb.12:33: Sell your possessions and give to the poor. Provide yourselves with purses that will not wear out, an inexhaustible treasure in heaven, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.
bsb.12:34: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
bsb.12:35: Be dressed for service and keep your lamps burning.
bsb.12:36: Then you will be like servants waiting for their master to return from the wedding banquet, so that when he comes and knocks, they can open the door for him at once.
bsb.12:37: Blessed are those servants whom the master finds on watch when he returns. Truly I tell you, he will dress himself to serve and will have them recline at the table, and he himself will come and wait on them.
bsb.12:38: Even if he comes in the second or third watch of the night and finds them alert, those servants will be blessed.
bsb.12:39: But understand this: If the homeowner had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have let his house be broken into.
bsb.12:40: You also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.”
bsb.12:41: “Lord,” said Peter, “are You addressing this parable to us, or to everyone else as well?”
bsb.12:42: And the Lord answered, “Who then is the faithful and wise manager, whom the master puts in charge of his servants to give them their portion at the proper time?
bsb.12:43: Blessed is that servant whose master finds him doing so when he returns.
bsb.12:44: Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.
bsb.12:45: But suppose that servant says in his heart, ‘My master will be a long time in coming,’ and he begins to beat the menservants and maidservants, and to eat and drink and get drunk.
bsb.12:46: The master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not anticipate. Then he will cut him to pieces and assign him a place with the unbelievers.
bsb.12:47: That servant who knows his master’s will but does not get ready or follow his instructions will be beaten with many blows.
bsb.12:48: But the one who unknowingly does things worthy of punishment will be beaten with few blows. From everyone who has been given much, much will be required; and from him who has been entrusted with much, even more will be demanded.
bsb.12:49: I have come to ignite a fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!
bsb.12:50: But I have a baptism to undergo, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!
bsb.12:51: Do you think that I have come to bring peace to the earth? No, I tell you, but division.
bsb.12:52: From now on, five in one household will be divided, three against two and two against three.
bsb.12:53: They will be divided, father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law.”
bsb.12:54: Then Jesus said to the crowds, “As soon as you see a cloud rising in the west, you say, ‘A shower is coming,’ and that is what happens.
bsb.12:55: And when the south wind blows, you say, ‘It will be hot,’ and it is.
bsb.12:56: You hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and sky. Why don’t you know how to interpret the present time?
bsb.12:57: And why don’t you judge for yourselves what is right?
bsb.12:58: Make every effort to reconcile with your adversary while you are on your way to the magistrate. Otherwise, he may drag you off to the judge, and the judge may hand you over to the officer, and the officer may throw you into prison.
bsb.12:59: I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the very last penny.”
bsb.13:1: At that time some of those present told Jesus about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
bsb.13:2: To this He replied, “Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered this fate?
bsb.13:3: No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you too will all perish.
bsb.13:4: Or those eighteen who were killed when the tower of Siloam collapsed on them: Do you think that they were more sinful than all the others living in Jerusalem?
bsb.13:5: No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you too will all perish.”
bsb.13:6: Then Jesus told this parable: “A man had a fig tree that was planted in his vineyard. He went to look for fruit on it, but did not find any.
bsb.13:7: So he said to the keeper of the vineyard, ‘Look, for the past three years I have come to search for fruit on this fig tree and haven’t found any. Therefore cut it down! Why should it use up the soil?’
bsb.13:8: ‘Sir,’ the man replied, ‘leave it alone again this year, until I dig around it and fertilize it.
bsb.13:9: If it bears fruit next year, fine. But if not, you can cut it down.’”
bsb.13:10: One Sabbath Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues,
bsb.13:11: and a woman there had been disabled by a spirit for eighteen years. She was hunched over and could not stand up straight.
bsb.13:12: When Jesus saw her, He called her over and said, “Woman, you are set free from your disability.”
bsb.13:13: Then He placed His hands on her, and immediately she straightened up and began to glorify God.
bsb.13:14: But the synagogue leader was indignant that Jesus had healed on the Sabbath. “There are six days for work,” he told the crowd. “So come and be healed on those days and not on the Sabbath.”
bsb.13:15: “You hypocrites!” the Lord replied. “Does not each of you on the Sabbath untie his ox or donkey from the stall and lead it to water?
bsb.13:16: Then should not this daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has kept bound for eighteen long years, be released from her bondage on the Sabbath day?”
bsb.13:17: When Jesus said this, all His adversaries were humiliated. And the whole crowd rejoiced at all the glorious things He was doing.
bsb.13:18: Then Jesus asked, “What is the kingdom of God like? To what can I compare it?
bsb.13:19: It is like a mustard seed that a man tossed into his garden. It grew and became a tree, and the birds of the air nested in its branches.”
bsb.13:20: Again He asked, “To what can I compare the kingdom of God?
bsb.13:21: It is like leaven that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until all of it was leavened.”
bsb.13:22: Then Jesus traveled throughout the towns and villages, teaching as He made His way toward Jerusalem.
bsb.13:23: “Lord,” someone asked Him, “will only a few people be saved?” Jesus answered,
bsb.13:24: “Make every effort to enter through the narrow door. For many, I tell you, will try to enter and will not be able.
bsb.13:25: After the master of the house gets up and shuts the door, you will stand outside knocking and saying, ‘Lord, open the door for us.’ But he will reply, ‘I do not know where you are from.’
bsb.13:26: Then you will say, ‘We ate and drank with you, and you taught in our streets.’
bsb.13:27: And he will answer, ‘I tell you, I do not know where you are from. Depart from me, all you evildoers.’
bsb.13:28: There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but you yourselves are thrown out.
bsb.13:29: People will come from east and west and north and south, and will recline at the table in the kingdom of God.
bsb.13:30: And indeed, some who are last will be first, and some who are first will be last.”
bsb.13:31: At that very hour, some Pharisees came to Jesus and told Him, “Leave this place and get away, because Herod wants to kill You.”
bsb.13:32: But Jesus replied, “Go tell that fox, ‘Look, I will keep driving out demons and healing people today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will reach My goal.’
bsb.13:33: Nevertheless, I must keep going today and tomorrow and the next day, for it is not admissible for a prophet to perish outside of Jerusalem.
bsb.13:34: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, how often I have longed to gather your children together as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!
bsb.13:35: Look, your house is left to you desolate. And I tell you that you will not see Me again until you say, ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.’”
bsb.14:1: One Sabbath, Jesus went to eat in the home of a leading Pharisee, and those in attendance were watching Him closely.
bsb.14:2: Right there before Him was a man with dropsy.
bsb.14:3: So Jesus asked the experts in the law and the Pharisees, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath or not?”
bsb.14:4: But they remained silent. Then Jesus took hold of the man, healed him, and sent him on his way.
bsb.14:5: And He asked them, “Which of you whose son or ox falls into a pit on the Sabbath day will not immediately pull him out?”
bsb.14:6: And they were unable to answer these questions.
bsb.14:7: When Jesus noticed how the guests chose the places of honor, He told them a parable:
bsb.14:8: “When you are invited to a wedding banquet, do not sit in the place of honor, in case someone more distinguished than you has been invited.
bsb.14:9: Then the host who invited both of you will come and tell you, ‘Give this man your seat.’ And in humiliation, you will have to take the last place.
bsb.14:10: But when you are invited, go and sit in the last place, so that your host will come and tell you, ‘Friend, move up to a better place.’ Then you will be honored in front of everyone at the table with you.
bsb.14:11: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”
bsb.14:12: Then Jesus said to the man who had invited Him, “When you host a dinner or a banquet, do not invite your friends or brothers or relatives or rich neighbors. Otherwise, they may invite you in return, and you will be repaid.
bsb.14:13: But when you host a banquet, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind,
bsb.14:14: and you will be blessed. Since they cannot repay you, you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.”
bsb.14:15: When one of those reclining with Him heard this, he said to Jesus, “Blessed is everyone who will eat at the feast in the kingdom of God.”
bsb.14:16: But Jesus replied, “A certain man prepared a great banquet and invited many guests.
bsb.14:17: When it was time for the banquet, he sent his servant to tell those who had been invited, ‘Come, for everything is now ready.’
bsb.14:18: But one after another they all began to make excuses. The first one said, ‘I have bought a field, and I need to go see it. Please excuse me.’
bsb.14:19: Another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to try them out. Please excuse me.’
bsb.14:20: Still another said, ‘I have married a wife, so I cannot come.’
bsb.14:21: The servant returned and reported all this to his master. Then the owner of the house became angry and said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and alleys of the city, and bring in the poor, the crippled, the blind, and the lame.’
bsb.14:22: ‘Sir,’ the servant replied, ‘what you ordered has been done, and there is still room.’
bsb.14:23: So the master told his servant, ‘Go out to the highways and hedges and compel them to come in, so that my house will be full.
bsb.14:24: For I tell you, not one of those men who were invited will taste my banquet.’”
bsb.14:25: Large crowds were now traveling with Jesus, and He turned and said to them,
bsb.14:26: “If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters—yes, even his own life—he cannot be My disciple.
bsb.14:27: And whoever does not carry his cross and follow Me cannot be My disciple.
bsb.14:28: Which of you, wishing to build a tower, does not first sit down and count the cost to see if he has the resources to complete it?
bsb.14:29: Otherwise, if he lays the foundation and is unable to finish the work, everyone who sees it will ridicule him,
bsb.14:30: saying, ‘This man could not finish what he started to build.’
bsb.14:31: Or what king on his way to war with another king will not first sit down and consider whether he can engage with ten thousand men the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
bsb.14:32: And if he is unable, he will send a delegation while the other king is still far off, to ask for terms of peace.
bsb.14:33: In the same way, any one of you who does not give up everything he has cannot be My disciple.
bsb.14:34: Salt is good, but if the salt loses its savor, with what will it be seasoned?
bsb.14:35: It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile, and it is thrown out. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”
bsb.15:1: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were gathering around to listen to Jesus.
bsb.15:2: So the Pharisees and scribes began to grumble: “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.”
bsb.15:3: Then Jesus told them this parable:
bsb.15:4: “What man among you, if he has a hundred sheep and loses one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the pasture and go after the one that is lost, until he finds it?
bsb.15:5: And when he finds it, he joyfully puts it on his shoulders,
bsb.15:6: comes home, and calls together his friends and neighbors to tell them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost sheep!’
bsb.15:7: In the same way, I tell you that there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous ones who do not need to repent.
bsb.15:8: Or what woman who has ten silver coins and loses one of them does not light a lamp, sweep her house, and search carefully until she finds it?
bsb.15:9: And when she finds it, she calls together her friends and neighbors to say, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost coin.’
bsb.15:10: In the same way, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of God’s angels over one sinner who repents.”
bsb.15:11: Then Jesus said, “There was a man who had two sons.
bsb.15:12: The younger son said to him, ‘Father, give me my share of the estate.’ So he divided his property between them.
bsb.15:13: After a few days, the younger son got everything together and journeyed to a distant country, where he squandered his wealth in wild living.
bsb.15:14: After he had spent all he had, a severe famine swept through that country, and he began to be in need.
bsb.15:15: So he went and hired himself out to a citizen of that country, who sent him into his fields to feed the pigs.
bsb.15:16: He longed to fill his belly with the pods the pigs were eating, but no one would give him a thing.
bsb.15:17: Finally he came to his senses and said, ‘How many of my father’s hired servants have plenty of food? But here I am, starving to death!
bsb.15:18: I will get up and go back to my father and say to him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you.
bsb.15:19: I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired servants.”’
bsb.15:20: So he got up and went to his father. But while he was still in the distance, his father saw him and was filled with compassion. He ran to his son, embraced him, and kissed him.
bsb.15:21: The son declared, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’
bsb.15:22: But the father said to his servants, ‘Quick! Bring the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet.
bsb.15:23: Bring the fattened calf and kill it. Let us feast and celebrate.
bsb.15:24: For this son of mine was dead and is alive again! He was lost and is found!’ So they began to celebrate.
bsb.15:25: Meanwhile the older son was in the field, and as he approached the house, he heard music and dancing.
bsb.15:26: So he called one of the servants and asked what was going on.
bsb.15:27: ‘Your brother has returned,’ he said, ‘and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has him back safe and sound.’
bsb.15:28: The older son became angry and refused to go in. So his father came out and pleaded with him.
bsb.15:29: But he answered his father, ‘Look, all these years I have served you and never disobeyed a commandment of yours. Yet you never gave me even a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends.
bsb.15:30: But when this son of yours returns from squandering your wealth with prostitutes, you kill the fattened calf for him!’
bsb.15:31: ‘Son, you are always with me,’ the father said, ‘and all that is mine is yours.
bsb.15:32: But it was fitting to celebrate and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.’”
bsb.16:1: Jesus also said to His disciples, “There was a rich man whose manager was accused of wasting his possessions.
bsb.16:2: So he called him in to ask, ‘What is this I hear about you? Turn in an account of your management, for you cannot be manager any longer.’
bsb.16:3: The manager said to himself, ‘What shall I do, now that my master is taking away my position? I am too weak to dig and too ashamed to beg.
bsb.16:4: I know what I will do, so that after my removal from management, people will welcome me into their homes.’
bsb.16:5: And he called in each one of his master’s debtors. ‘How much do you owe my master?’ he asked the first.
bsb.16:6: ‘A hundred measures of olive oil,’ he answered. ‘Take your bill,’ said the manager. ‘Sit down quickly, and write fifty.’
bsb.16:7: Then he asked another, ‘And how much do you owe?’ ‘A hundred measures of wheat,’ he replied. ‘Take your bill and write eighty,’ he told him.
bsb.16:8: The master commended the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly. For the sons of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than are the sons of light.
bsb.16:9: I tell you, use worldly wealth to make friends for yourselves, so that when it is gone, they will welcome you into eternal dwellings.
bsb.16:10: Whoever is faithful with very little will also be faithful with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.
bsb.16:11: So if you have not been faithful with worldly wealth, who will entrust you with true riches?
bsb.16:12: And if you have not been faithful with the belongings of another, who will give you belongings of your own?
bsb.16:13: No servant can serve two masters. Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.”
bsb.16:14: The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all of this and were scoffing at Jesus.
bsb.16:15: So He said to them, “You are the ones who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts. For what is prized among men is detestable before God.
bsb.16:16: The Law and the Prophets were proclaimed until John. Since that time, the gospel of the kingdom of God is being preached, and everyone is forcing his way into it.
bsb.16:17: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for a single stroke of a pen to drop out of the Law.
bsb.16:18: Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery, and he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
bsb.16:19: Now there was a rich man dressed in purple and fine linen, who lived each day in joyous splendor.
bsb.16:20: And a beggar named Lazarus lay at his gate, covered with sores
