bsb.16:21: and longing to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.
bsb.16:22: One day the beggar died and was carried by the angels to Abraham’s side. And the rich man also died and was buried.
bsb.16:23: In Hades, where he was in torment, he looked up and saw Abraham from afar, with Lazarus by his side.
bsb.16:24: So he cried out, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue. For I am in agony in this fire.’
bsb.16:25: But Abraham answered, ‘Child, remember that during your lifetime you received your good things, while Lazarus received bad things. But now he is comforted here, while you are in agony.
bsb.16:26: And besides all this, a great chasm has been fixed between us and you, so that even those who wish cannot cross from here to you, nor can anyone cross from there to us.’
bsb.16:27: ‘Then I beg you, father,’ he said, ‘send Lazarus to my father’s house,
bsb.16:28: for I have five brothers. Let him warn them, so that they will not also end up in this place of torment.’
bsb.16:29: But Abraham replied, ‘They have Moses and the prophets; let your brothers listen to them.’
bsb.16:30: ‘No, father Abraham,’ he said, ‘but if someone is sent to them from the dead, they will repent.’
bsb.16:31: Then Abraham said to him, ‘If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, they will not be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead.’”
bsb.17:1: Jesus said to His disciples, “It is inevitable that stumbling blocks will come, but woe to the one through whom they come!
bsb.17:2: It would be better for him to have a millstone hung around his neck and to be thrown into the sea than to cause one of these little ones to stumble.
bsb.17:3: Watch yourselves. If your brother sins, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.
bsb.17:4: Even if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times returns to say, ‘I repent,’ you must forgive him.”
bsb.17:5: The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith!”
bsb.17:6: And the Lord answered, “If you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you can say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea,’ and it will obey you.
bsb.17:7: Which of you whose servant comes in from plowing or shepherding in the field will say to him, ‘Come at once and sit down to eat’?
bsb.17:8: Instead, won’t he tell him, ‘Prepare my meal and dress yourself to serve me while I eat and drink; and afterward you may eat and drink’?
bsb.17:9: Does he thank the servant because he did what he was told?
bsb.17:10: So you also, when you have done everything commanded of you, should say, ‘We are unworthy servants; we have only done our duty.’”
bsb.17:11: While Jesus was on His way to Jerusalem, He was passing between Samaria and Galilee.
bsb.17:12: As He entered one of the villages, He was met by ten lepers. They stood at a distance
bsb.17:13: and raised their voices, shouting, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”
bsb.17:14: When Jesus saw them, He said, “Go, show yourselves to the priests.” And as they were on their way, they were cleansed.
bsb.17:15: When one of them saw that he was healed, he came back, praising God in a loud voice.
bsb.17:16: He fell facedown at Jesus’ feet in thanksgiving to Him—and he was a Samaritan.
bsb.17:17: “Were not all ten cleansed?” Jesus asked. “Where then are the other nine?
bsb.17:18: Was no one found except this foreigner to return and give glory to God?”
bsb.17:19: Then Jesus said to him, “Rise and go; your faith has made you well!”
bsb.17:20: When asked by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God would come, Jesus replied, “The kingdom of God will not come with observable signs.
bsb.17:21: Nor will people say, ‘Look, here it is,’ or ‘There it is.’ For you see, the kingdom of God is in your midst.”
bsb.17:22: Then He said to the disciples, “The time is coming when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, but you will not see it.
bsb.17:23: People will tell you, ‘Look, there He is!’ or ‘Look, here He is!’ Do not go out or chase after them.
bsb.17:24: For just as the lightning flashes and lights up the sky from one end to the other, so will be the Son of Man in His day.
bsb.17:25: But first He must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
bsb.17:26: Just as it was in the days of Noah, so also will it be in the days of the Son of Man:
bsb.17:27: People were eating and drinking, marrying and being given in marriage, up to the day Noah entered the ark. Then the flood came and destroyed them all.
bsb.17:28: It was the same in the days of Lot: People were eating and drinking, buying and selling, planting and building.
bsb.17:29: But on the day Lot left Sodom, fire and sulfur rained down from heaven and destroyed them all.
bsb.17:30: It will be just like that on the day the Son of Man is revealed.
bsb.17:31: On that day, let no one on the housetop come down to retrieve his possessions. Likewise, let no one in the field return for anything he has left behind.
bsb.17:33: Whoever tries to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life will preserve it.
bsb.17:34: I tell you, on that night two people will be in one bed: one will be taken and the other left.
bsb.17:35: Two women will be grinding grain together: one will be taken and the other left.”
bsb.17:37: “Where, Lord?” they asked. Jesus answered, “Wherever there is a carcass, there the vultures will gather.”
bsb.18:1: Then Jesus told them a parable about their need to pray at all times and not lose heart:
bsb.18:2: “In a certain town there was a judge who neither feared God nor respected men.
bsb.18:3: And there was a widow in that town who kept appealing to him, ‘Give me justice against my adversary.’
bsb.18:4: For a while he refused, but later he said to himself, ‘Though I neither fear God nor respect men,
bsb.18:5: yet because this widow keeps pestering me, I will give her justice. Then she will stop wearing me out with her perpetual requests.’”
bsb.18:6: And the Lord said, “Listen to the words of the unjust judge.
bsb.18:7: Will not God bring about justice for His elect who cry out to Him day and night? Will He continue to defer their help?
bsb.18:8: I tell you, He will promptly carry out justice on their behalf. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will He find faith on earth?”
bsb.18:9: To some who trusted in their own righteousness and viewed others with contempt, He also told this parable:
bsb.18:10: “Two men went up to the temple to pray. One was a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
bsb.18:11: The Pharisee stood by himself and prayed, ‘God, I thank You that I am not like the other men—swindlers, evildoers, adulterers—or even like this tax collector.
bsb.18:12: I fast twice a week and pay tithes of all that I acquire.’
bsb.18:13: But the tax collector stood at a distance, unwilling even to lift up his eyes to heaven. Instead, he beat his breast and said, ‘God, have mercy on me, a sinner!’
bsb.18:14: I tell you, this man, rather than the Pharisee, went home justified. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”
bsb.18:15: Now people were even bringing their babies to Jesus for Him to place His hands on them. And when the disciples saw this, they rebuked those who brought them.
bsb.18:16: But Jesus called the children to Him and said, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
bsb.18:17: Truly I tell you, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.”
bsb.18:18: Then a certain ruler asked Him, “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
bsb.18:19: “Why do you call Me good?” Jesus replied. “No one is good except God alone.
bsb.18:20: You know the commandments: ‘Do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honor your father and mother.’”
bsb.18:21: “All these I have kept from my youth,” he said.
bsb.18:22: On hearing this, Jesus told him, “You still lack one thing: Sell everything you own and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.”
bsb.18:23: But when the ruler heard this, he became very sad, because he was extremely wealthy.
bsb.18:24: Seeing the man’s sadness, Jesus said, “How hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God!
bsb.18:25: Indeed, it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.”
bsb.18:26: Those who heard this asked, “Who then can be saved?”
bsb.18:27: But Jesus said, “What is impossible with man is possible with God.”
bsb.18:28: “Look,” said Peter, “we have left all we had to follow You.”
bsb.18:29: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “no one who has left home or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
bsb.18:30: will fail to receive many times more in this age—and in the age to come, eternal life.”
bsb.18:31: Then Jesus took the Twelve aside and said to them, “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything the prophets have written about the Son of Man will be fulfilled.
bsb.18:32: He will be delivered over to the Gentiles and will be mocked and insulted and spit upon.
bsb.18:33: They will flog Him and kill Him, and on the third day He will rise again.”
bsb.18:34: But the disciples did not understand any of these things. The meaning was hidden from them, and they did not comprehend what He was saying.
bsb.18:35: As Jesus drew near to Jericho, a blind man was sitting beside the road, begging.
bsb.18:36: When he heard the crowd going by, he asked what was happening.
bsb.18:37: “Jesus of Nazareth is passing by,” they told him.
bsb.18:38: So he called out, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
bsb.18:39: Those who led the way admonished him to be silent, but he cried out all the louder, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
bsb.18:40: Jesus stopped and directed that the man be brought to Him. When he had been brought near, Jesus asked him,
bsb.18:41: “What do you want Me to do for you?” “Lord,” he said, “let me see again.”
bsb.18:42: “Receive your sight!” Jesus replied. “Your faith has healed you.”
bsb.18:43: Immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus, glorifying God. And all the people who saw this gave praise to God.
bsb.19:1: Then Jesus entered Jericho and was passing through.
bsb.19:2: And there was a man named Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector, who was very wealthy.
bsb.19:3: He was trying to see who Jesus was, but could not see over the crowd because he was small in stature.
bsb.19:4: So he ran on ahead and climbed a sycamore tree to see Him, since Jesus was about to pass that way.
bsb.19:5: When Jesus came to that place, He looked up and said, “Zacchaeus, hurry down, for I must stay at your house today.”
bsb.19:6: So Zacchaeus hurried down and welcomed Him joyfully.
bsb.19:7: And all who saw this began to grumble, saying, “He has gone to be the guest of a sinful man!”
bsb.19:8: But Zacchaeus stood up and said to the Lord, “Look, Lord, half of my possessions I give to the poor, and if I have cheated anyone, I will repay it fourfold.”
bsb.19:9: Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this house, because this man too is a son of Abraham.
bsb.19:10: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.”
bsb.19:11: While the people were listening to this, Jesus proceeded to tell them a parable, because He was near Jerusalem and they thought the kingdom of God would appear imminently.
bsb.19:12: So He said, “A man of noble birth went to a distant country to lay claim to his kingship and then return.
bsb.19:13: Beforehand, he called ten of his servants and gave them ten minas. ‘Conduct business with this until I return,’ he said.
bsb.19:14: But his subjects hated him and sent a delegation after him to say, ‘We do not want this man to rule over us.’
bsb.19:15: When he returned from procuring his kingship, he summoned the servants to whom he had given the money, to find out what each one had earned.
bsb.19:16: The first servant came forward and said, ‘Master, your mina has produced ten more minas.’
bsb.19:17: His master replied, ‘Well done, good servant! Because you have been faithful in a very small matter, you shall have authority over ten cities.’
bsb.19:18: The second servant came and said, ‘Master, your mina has made five minas.’
bsb.19:19: And to this one he said, ‘You shall have authority over five cities.’
bsb.19:20: Then another servant came and said, ‘Master, here is your mina, which I have laid away in a piece of cloth.
bsb.19:21: For I was afraid of you, because you are a harsh man. You withdraw what you did not deposit and reap what you did not sow.’
bsb.19:22: His master replied, ‘You wicked servant, I will judge you by your own words. So you knew that I am a harsh man, withdrawing what I did not deposit and reaping what I did not sow?
bsb.19:23: Why then did you not deposit my money in the bank, and upon my return I could have collected it with interest?’
bsb.19:24: Then he told those standing by, ‘Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.’
bsb.19:26: He replied, ‘I tell you that everyone who has will be given more; but the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
bsb.19:27: And these enemies of mine who were unwilling for me to rule over them, bring them here and slay them in front of me.’”
bsb.19:28: After Jesus had said this, He went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
bsb.19:29: As He approached Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, He sent out two of His disciples,
bsb.19:30: saying, “Go into the village ahead of you, and as you enter it, you will find a colt tied there, on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it here.
bsb.19:31: If anyone asks, ‘Why are you untying it?’ tell him, ‘The Lord needs it.’”
bsb.19:32: So those who were sent went out and found it just as Jesus had told them.
bsb.19:33: As they were untying the colt, its owners asked, “Why are you untying the colt?”
bsb.19:35: Then they led the colt to Jesus, threw their cloaks over it, and put Jesus on it.
bsb.19:36: As He rode along, the people spread their cloaks on the road.
bsb.19:37: And as He approached the descent from the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of disciples began to praise God joyfully in a loud voice for all the miracles they had seen:
bsb.19:38: “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord!” “Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!”
bsb.19:39: But some of the Pharisees in the crowd said to Him, “Teacher, rebuke Your disciples!”
bsb.19:40: “I tell you,” He answered, “if they remain silent, the very stones will cry out.”
bsb.19:41: As Jesus approached Jerusalem and saw the city, He wept over it
bsb.19:42: and said, “If only you had known on this day what would bring you peace! But now it is hidden from your eyes.
bsb.19:43: For the days will come upon you when your enemies will barricade you and surround you and hem you in on every side.
bsb.19:44: They will level you to the ground—you and the children within your walls. They will not leave one stone on another, because you did not recognize the time of your visitation from God.”
bsb.19:45: Then Jesus entered the temple courts and began to drive out those who were selling there.
bsb.19:46: He declared to them, “It is written: ‘My house will be a house of prayer.’ But you have made it ‘a den of robbers.’”
bsb.19:47: Jesus was teaching at the temple every day, but the chief priests, scribes, and leaders of the people were intent on killing Him.
bsb.19:48: Yet they could not find a way to do so, because all the people hung on His words.
bsb.20:1: One day as Jesus was teaching the people in the temple courts and proclaiming the gospel, the chief priests and scribes, together with the elders, came up to Him.
bsb.20:2: “Tell us,” they said, “by what authority are You doing these things, and who gave You this authority?”
bsb.20:3: “I will also ask you a question,” Jesus replied. “Tell Me:
bsb.20:4: John’s baptism—was it from heaven, or from men?”
bsb.20:5: They deliberated among themselves and said, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask, ‘Why did you not believe him?’
bsb.20:6: But if we say, ‘From men,’ all the people will stone us, for they are convinced that John was a prophet.”
bsb.20:7: So they answered that they did not know where it was from.
bsb.20:8: And Jesus replied, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.”
bsb.20:9: Then He proceeded to tell the people this parable: “A man planted a vineyard, rented it out to some tenants, and went away for a long time.
bsb.20:10: At harvest time, he sent a servant to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard. But the tenants beat the servant and sent him away empty-handed.
bsb.20:11: So he sent another servant, but they beat him and treated him shamefully, sending him away empty-handed.
bsb.20:12: Then he sent a third, but they wounded him and threw him out.
bsb.20:13: ‘What shall I do?’ asked the owner of the vineyard. ‘I will send my beloved son. Perhaps they will respect him.’
bsb.20:14: But when the tenants saw the son, they discussed it among themselves and said, ‘This is the heir. Let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
bsb.20:15: So they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. What then will the owner of the vineyard do to them?
bsb.20:16: He will come and kill those tenants, and will give the vineyard to others.” And when the people heard this, they said, “May such a thing never happen!”
bsb.20:17: But Jesus looked directly at them and said, “Then what is the meaning of that which is written: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone’?
bsb.20:18: Everyone who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but he on whom it falls will be crushed.”
bsb.20:19: When the scribes and chief priests realized that Jesus had spoken this parable against them, they sought to arrest Him that very hour. But they were afraid of the people.
bsb.20:20: So they watched Him closely and sent spies who pretended to be sincere. They were hoping to catch Him in His words in order to hand Him over to the rule and authority of the governor.
bsb.20:21: “Teacher,” they inquired, “we know that You speak and teach correctly. You show no partiality, but teach the way of God in accordance with the truth.
bsb.20:22: Is it lawful for us to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”
bsb.20:23: But Jesus saw through their duplicity and said to them,
bsb.20:24: “Show Me a denarius. Whose image and inscription are on it?” “Caesar’s,” they answered.
bsb.20:25: So Jesus told them, “Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.”
bsb.20:26: And they were unable to trap Him in His words before the people; and amazed at His answer, they fell silent.
bsb.20:27: Then some of the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to question Him.
bsb.20:28: “Teacher,” they said, “Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife but no children, the man is to marry his brother’s widow and raise up offspring for him.
bsb.20:29: Now there were seven brothers. The first one married a wife, but died childless.
bsb.20:31: and the third married the widow, and in the same way all seven died, leaving no children.
bsb.20:32: And last of all, the woman died.
bsb.20:33: So then, in the resurrection, whose wife will she be? For all seven were married to her.”
bsb.20:34: Jesus answered, “The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage.
bsb.20:35: But those who are considered worthy to share in the age to come and in the resurrection from the dead will neither marry nor be given in marriage.
bsb.20:36: In fact, they can no longer die, because they are like the angels. And since they are sons of the resurrection, they are sons of God.
bsb.20:37: Even Moses demonstrates that the dead are raised, in the passage about the burning bush. For he calls the Lord ‘the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’
bsb.20:38: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living, for to Him all are alive.”
bsb.20:39: Some of the scribes answered, “Teacher, You have spoken well!”
bsb.20:40: And they did not dare to question Him any further.
bsb.20:41: Then Jesus declared, “How can it be said that the Christ is the Son of David?
bsb.20:42: For David himself says in the book of Psalms: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand
bsb.20:43: until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.”’
bsb.20:44: Thus David calls Him ‘Lord.’ So how can He be David’s son?”
bsb.20:45: In the hearing of all the people, Jesus said to His disciples,
bsb.20:46: “Beware of the scribes. They like to walk around in long robes, and they love the greetings in the marketplaces, the chief seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at banquets.
bsb.20:47: They defraud widows of their houses, and for a show make lengthy prayers. These men will receive greater condemnation.”
bsb.21:1: Then Jesus looked up and saw the rich putting their gifts into the treasury,
bsb.21:2: and He saw a poor widow put in two small copper coins.
bsb.21:3: “Truly I tell you,” He said, “this poor widow has put in more than all the others.
bsb.21:4: For they all contributed out of their surplus, but she out of her poverty has put in all she had to live on.”
bsb.21:5: As some of the disciples were remarking how the temple was adorned with beautiful stones and consecrated gifts, Jesus said,
bsb.21:6: “As for what you see here, the time will come when not one stone will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.”
bsb.21:7: “Teacher,” they asked, “when will these things happen? And what will be the sign that they are about to take place?”
bsb.21:8: Jesus answered, “See to it that you are not deceived. For many will come in My name, claiming, ‘I am He,’ and, ‘The time is near.’ Do not follow them.
bsb.21:9: When you hear of wars and rebellions, do not be alarmed. These things must happen first, but the end is not imminent.”
bsb.21:10: Then He told them, “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
bsb.21:11: There will be great earthquakes, famines, and pestilences in various places, along with fearful sights and great signs from heaven.
bsb.21:12: But before all this, they will seize you and persecute you. On account of My name they will deliver you to the synagogues and prisons, and they will bring you before kings and governors.
bsb.21:13: This will be your opportunity to serve as witnesses.
bsb.21:14: So make up your mind not to worry beforehand how to defend yourselves.
bsb.21:15: For I will give you speech and wisdom that none of your adversaries will be able to resist or contradict.
bsb.21:16: You will be betrayed even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and some of you will be put to death.
bsb.21:17: And you will be hated by everyone because of My name.
bsb.21:18: Yet not even a hair of your head will perish.
bsb.21:19: By your patient endurance you will gain your souls.
bsb.21:20: But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, you will know that her desolation is near.
bsb.21:21: Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains, let those in the city get out, and let those in the country stay out of the city.
bsb.21:22: For these are the days of vengeance, to fulfill all that is written.
bsb.21:23: How miserable those days will be for pregnant and nursing mothers! For there will be great distress upon the land and wrath against this people.
bsb.21:24: They will fall by the edge of the sword and be led captive into all the nations. And Jerusalem will be trodden down by the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
bsb.21:25: There will be signs in the sun and moon and stars, and on the earth dismay among the nations, bewildered by the roaring of the sea and the surging of the waves.
bsb.21:26: Men will faint from fear and anxiety over what is coming upon the earth, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
bsb.21:27: At that time they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
bsb.21:28: When these things begin to happen, stand up and lift up your heads, because your redemption is drawing near.”
bsb.21:29: Then Jesus told them a parable: “Look at the fig tree and all the trees.
bsb.21:30: When they sprout leaves, you can see for yourselves and know that summer is near.
bsb.21:31: So also, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.
bsb.21:32: Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things have happened.
bsb.21:33: Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away.
bsb.21:34: But watch yourselves, or your hearts will be weighed down by dissipation, drunkenness, and the worries of life—and that day will spring upon you suddenly like a snare.
bsb.21:35: For it will come upon all who dwell on the face of all the earth.
bsb.21:36: So keep watch at all times, and pray that you may have the strength to escape all that is about to happen and to stand before the Son of Man.”
bsb.21:37: Every day Jesus taught at the temple, but every evening He went out to spend the night on the Mount of Olives.
bsb.21:38: And early in the morning all the people would come to hear Him at the temple.
bsb.22:1: Now the Feast of Unleavened Bread, called the Passover, was approaching,
bsb.22:2: and the chief priests and scribes were looking for a way to put Jesus to death; for they feared the people.
bsb.22:3: Then Satan entered Judas Iscariot, who was one of the Twelve.
bsb.22:4: And Judas went to discuss with the chief priests and temple officers how he might betray Jesus to them.
bsb.22:5: They were delighted and agreed to give him money.
bsb.22:6: Judas consented, and began to look for an opportunity to betray Jesus to them in the absence of a crowd.
bsb.22:7: Then came the day of Unleavened Bread on which the Passover lamb was to be sacrificed.
bsb.22:8: Jesus sent Peter and John, saying, “Go and prepare for us to eat the Passover.”
bsb.22:9: “Where do You want us to prepare it?” they asked.
bsb.22:10: He answered, “When you enter the city, a man carrying a jug of water will meet you. Follow him to the house he enters,
bsb.22:11: and say to the owner of that house, ‘The Teacher asks: Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with My disciples?’
bsb.22:12: And he will show you a large upper room, already furnished. Make preparations there.”
bsb.22:13: So they went and found it just as Jesus had told them. And they prepared the Passover.
bsb.22:14: When the hour had come, Jesus reclined at the table with His apostles.
bsb.22:15: And He said to them, “I have eagerly desired to eat this Passover with you before My suffering.
bsb.22:16: For I tell you that I will not eat it again until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.”
bsb.22:17: After taking the cup, He gave thanks and said, “Take this and divide it among yourselves.
bsb.22:18: For I tell you that I will not drink of the fruit of the vine from now on until the kingdom of God comes.”
bsb.22:19: And He took the bread, gave thanks and broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “This is My body, given for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”
bsb.22:20: In the same way, after supper He took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is poured out for you.
bsb.22:21: Look! The hand of My betrayer is with Mine on the table.
bsb.22:22: Indeed, the Son of Man will go as it has been determined, but woe to that man who betrays Him.”
bsb.22:23: Then they began to question among themselves which of them was going to do this.
bsb.22:24: A dispute also arose among the disciples as to which of them would be considered the greatest.
bsb.22:25: So Jesus declared, “The kings of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those in authority over them call themselves benefactors.
bsb.22:26: But you shall not be like them. Instead, the greatest among you should be like the youngest, and the one who leads like the one who serves.
bsb.22:27: For who is greater, the one who reclines at the table or the one who serves? Is it not the one who reclines? But I am among you as one who serves.
bsb.22:28: You are the ones who have stood by Me in My trials.
bsb.22:29: And I bestow on you a kingdom, just as My Father has bestowed one on Me,
bsb.22:30: so that you may eat and drink at My table in My kingdom, and sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
bsb.22:31: Simon, Simon, Satan has asked to sift each of you like wheat.
bsb.22:32: But I have prayed for you, Simon, that your faith will not fail. And when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.”
bsb.22:33: “Lord,” said Peter, “I am ready to go with You even to prison and to death.”
bsb.22:34: But Jesus replied, “I tell you, Peter, the rooster will not crow today until you have denied three times that you know Me.”
bsb.22:35: Then Jesus asked them, “When I sent you out without purse or bag or sandals, did you lack anything?” “Nothing,” they answered.
bsb.22:36: “Now, however,” He told them, “the one with a purse should take it, and likewise a bag; and the one without a sword should sell his cloak and buy one.
bsb.22:37: For I tell you that this Scripture must be fulfilled in Me: ‘And He was numbered with the transgressors.’ For what is written about Me is reaching its fulfillment.”
bsb.22:38: So they said, “Look, Lord, here are two swords.” “That is enough,” He answered.
bsb.22:39: Jesus went out as usual to the Mount of Olives, and the disciples followed Him.
bsb.22:40: When He came to the place, He told them, “Pray that you will not enter into temptation.”
bsb.22:41: And He withdrew about a stone’s throw beyond them, where He knelt down and prayed,
bsb.22:42: “Father, if You are willing, take this cup from Me. Yet not My will, but Yours be done.”
bsb.22:43: Then an angel from heaven appeared to Him and strengthened Him.
bsb.22:44: And in His anguish, He prayed more earnestly, and His sweat became like drops of blood falling to the ground.
bsb.22:45: When Jesus rose from prayer and returned to the disciples, He found them asleep, exhausted from sorrow.
bsb.22:46: “Why are you sleeping?” He asked. “Get up and pray so that you will not enter into temptation.”
bsb.22:47: While He was still speaking, a crowd arrived, led by the man called Judas, one of the Twelve. He approached Jesus to kiss Him.
bsb.22:48: But Jesus asked him, “Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?”
bsb.22:49: Those around Jesus saw what was about to happen and said, “Lord, should we strike with our swords?”
bsb.22:50: And one of them struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his right ear.
bsb.22:51: But Jesus answered, “No more of this!” And He touched the man’s ear and healed him.
bsb.22:52: Then Jesus said to the chief priests, temple officers, and elders who had come for Him, “Have you come out with swords and clubs as you would against an outlaw?
bsb.22:53: Every day I was with you in the temple courts, and you did not lay a hand on Me. But this hour belongs to you and to the power of darkness.”
bsb.22:54: Then they seized Jesus, led Him away, and took Him into the house of the high priest. And Peter followed at a distance.
bsb.22:55: When those present had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down together, Peter sat down among them.
bsb.22:56: A servant girl saw him seated in the firelight and looked intently at him. “This man also was with Him,” she said.
bsb.22:57: But Peter denied it. “Woman, I do not know Him,” he said.
bsb.22:58: A short time later, someone else saw him and said, “You also are one of them.” But Peter said, “Man, I am not.”
bsb.22:59: About an hour later, another man insisted, “Certainly this man was with Him, for he too is a Galilean.”
bsb.22:60: “Man, I do not know what you are talking about,” Peter replied. While he was still speaking, the rooster crowed.
bsb.22:61: And the Lord turned and looked at Peter. Then Peter remembered the word that the Lord had spoken to him: “Before the rooster crows today, you will deny Me three times.”
bsb.22:62: And he went outside and wept bitterly.
bsb.22:63: The men who were holding Jesus began to mock Him and beat Him.
bsb.22:64: They blindfolded Him and kept demanding, “Prophesy! Who hit You?”
bsb.22:65: And they said many other blasphemous things against Him.
bsb.22:66: At daybreak the council of the elders of the people, both the chief priests and scribes, met together. They led Jesus into their Sanhedrin and said,
bsb.22:67: “If You are the Christ, tell us.” Jesus answered, “If I tell you, you will not believe.
bsb.22:68: And if I ask you a question, you will not answer.
bsb.22:69: But from now on the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God.”
bsb.22:70: So they all asked, “Are You then the Son of God?” He replied, “You say that I am.”
bsb.22:71: “Why do we need any more testimony?” they declared. “We have heard it for ourselves from His own lips.”
bsb.23:1: Then the whole council rose and led Jesus away to Pilate.
bsb.23:2: And they began to accuse Him, saying, “We found this man subverting our nation, forbidding payment of taxes to Caesar, and proclaiming Himself to be Christ, a King.”
bsb.23:3: So Pilate asked Him, “Are You the King of the Jews?” “You have said so,” Jesus replied.
bsb.23:4: Then Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds, “I find no basis for a charge against this man.”
bsb.23:5: But they kept insisting, “He stirs up the people all over Judea with His teaching. He began in Galilee and has come all the way here.”
bsb.23:6: When Pilate heard this, he asked if the man was a Galilean.
bsb.23:7: And learning that Jesus was under Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent Him to Herod, who himself was in Jerusalem at that time.
bsb.23:8: When Herod saw Jesus, he was greatly pleased. He had wanted to see Him for a long time, because he had heard about Him and was hoping to see Him perform a miracle.
bsb.23:9: Herod questioned Jesus at great length, but He gave no answer.
bsb.23:10: Meanwhile, the chief priests and scribes stood there, vehemently accusing Him.
bsb.23:11: And even Herod and his soldiers ridiculed and mocked Him. Dressing Him in a fine robe, they sent Him back to Pilate.
bsb.23:12: That day Herod and Pilate became friends; before this time they had been enemies.
bsb.23:13: Then Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people,
bsb.23:14: and said to them, “You brought me this man as one who was inciting the people to rebellion. I have examined Him here in your presence and found Him not guilty of your charges against Him.
bsb.23:15: Neither has Herod, for he sent Him back to us. As you can see, He has done nothing deserving of death.
bsb.23:16: Therefore I will punish Him and release Him.”
bsb.23:18: But they all cried out in unison: “Away with this man! Release Barabbas to us!”
bsb.23:19: (Barabbas had been imprisoned for an insurrection in the city, and for murder.)
bsb.23:20: Wanting to release Jesus, Pilate addressed them again,
bsb.23:21: but they kept shouting, “Crucify Him! Crucify Him!”
bsb.23:22: A third time he said to them, “What evil has this man done? I have found in Him no offense worthy of death. So after I punish Him, I will release Him.”
bsb.23:23: But they were insistent, demanding with loud voices for Jesus to be crucified. And their clamor prevailed.
bsb.23:24: So Pilate sentenced that their demand be met.
bsb.23:25: As they had requested, he released the one imprisoned for insurrection and murder, and handed Jesus over to their will.
bsb.23:26: As the soldiers led Him away, they seized Simon of Cyrene on his way in from the country, and put the cross on him to carry behind Jesus.
bsb.23:27: A great number of people followed Him, including women who kept mourning and wailing for Him.
bsb.23:28: But Jesus turned to them and said, “Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for Me, but weep for yourselves and for your children.
bsb.23:29: Look, the days are coming when people will say, ‘Blessed are the barren women, the wombs that never bore, and breasts that never nursed!’
bsb.23:30: At that time ‘they will say to the mountains, “Fall on us!” and to the hills, “Cover us!”’
bsb.23:31: For if men do these things while the tree is green, what will happen when it is dry?”
bsb.23:32: Two others, who were criminals, were also led away to be executed with Jesus.
bsb.23:33: When they came to the place called The Skull, they crucified Him there, along with the criminals, one on His right and the other on His left.
bsb.23:34: Then Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.” And they divided up His garments by casting lots.
bsb.23:35: The people stood watching, and the rulers sneered at Him, saying, “He saved others; let Him save Himself if He is the Christ of God, the Chosen One.”
bsb.23:36: The soldiers also mocked Him and came up to offer Him sour wine.
bsb.23:37: “If You are the King of the Jews,” they said, “save Yourself!”
bsb.23:38: Above Him was posted an inscription: THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
bsb.23:39: One of the criminals who hung there heaped abuse on Him. “Are You not the Christ?” he said. “Save Yourself and us!”
bsb.23:40: But the other one rebuked him, saying, “Do you not even fear God, since you are under the same judgment?
bsb.23:41: We are punished justly, for we are receiving what our actions deserve. But this man has done nothing wrong.”
bsb.23:42: Then he said, “Jesus, remember me when You come into Your kingdom!”
bsb.23:43: And Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you, today you will be with Me in Paradise.”
bsb.23:44: It was now about the sixth hour, and darkness came over all the land until the ninth hour.
bsb.23:45: The sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was torn down the middle.
bsb.23:46: Then Jesus called out in a loud voice, “Father, into Your hands I commit My Spirit.” And when He had said this, He breathed His last.
bsb.23:47: When the centurion saw what had happened, he gave glory to God, saying, “Surely this was a righteous man.”
bsb.23:48: And when all the people who had gathered for this spectacle saw what had happened, they returned home beating their breasts.
bsb.23:49: But all those who knew Jesus, including the women who had followed Him from Galilee, stood at a distance watching these things.
bsb.23:50: Now there was a Council member named Joseph, a good and righteous man,
bsb.23:51: who had not consented to their decision or action. He was from the Judean town of Arimathea, and was waiting for the kingdom of God.
bsb.23:52: He went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus.
bsb.23:53: Then he took it down, wrapped it in a linen cloth, and placed it in a tomb cut into the rock, where no one had yet been laid.
bsb.23:54: It was Preparation Day, and the Sabbath was beginning.
bsb.23:55: The women who had come with Jesus from Galilee followed, and they saw the tomb and how His body was placed.
bsb.23:56: Then they returned to prepare spices and perfumes. And they rested on the Sabbath, according to the commandment.
bsb.24:1: On the first day of the week, very early in the morning, the women came to the tomb, bringing the spices they had prepared.
bsb.24:2: They found the stone rolled away from the tomb,
bsb.24:3: but when they entered, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
bsb.24:4: While they were puzzling over this, suddenly two men in radiant apparel stood beside them.
bsb.24:5: As the women bowed their faces to the ground in terror, the two men asked them, “Why do you look for the living among the dead?
bsb.24:6: He is not here; He has risen! Remember how He told you while He was still in Galilee:
bsb.24:7: ‘The Son of Man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and on the third day rise again.’”
bsb.24:9: And when they returned from the tomb, they reported all these things to the Eleven and to all the others.
bsb.24:10: It was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the other women with them who told this to the apostles.
bsb.24:11: But their words seemed like nonsense to them, and they did not believe the women.
bsb.24:12: Peter, however, got up and ran to the tomb. And after bending down and seeing only the linen cloths, he went away, wondering to himself what had happened.
bsb.24:13: That same day two of them were going to a village called Emmaus, about seven miles from Jerusalem.
bsb.24:14: They were talking with each other about everything that had happened.
bsb.24:15: And as they talked and deliberated, Jesus Himself came up and walked along with them.
bsb.24:16: But their eyes were kept from recognizing Him.
bsb.24:17: He asked them, “What are you discussing so intently as you walk along?” They stood still, with sadness on their faces.
bsb.24:18: One of them, named Cleopas, asked Him, “Are You the only visitor to Jerusalem who does not know the things that have happened there in recent days?”
bsb.24:19: “What things?” He asked. “The events involving Jesus of Nazareth,” they answered. “This man was a prophet, powerful in speech and action before God and all the people.
bsb.24:20: Our chief priests and rulers delivered Him up to the sentence of death, and they crucified Him.
bsb.24:21: But we were hoping He was the One who would redeem Israel. And besides all this, it is the third day since these things took place.
bsb.24:22: Furthermore, some of our women astounded us. They were at the tomb early this morning,
bsb.24:23: but they did not find His body. They came and told us they had seen a vision of angels, who said that Jesus was alive.
bsb.24:24: Then some of our companions went to the tomb and found it just as the women had described. But Him they did not see.”
bsb.24:25: Then Jesus said to them, “O foolish ones, how slow are your hearts to believe all that the prophets have spoken!
bsb.24:26: Was it not necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and then to enter His glory?”
bsb.24:27: And beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, He explained to them what was written in all the Scriptures about Himself.
bsb.24:28: As they approached the village where they were headed, He seemed to be going farther.
bsb.24:29: But they pleaded with Him, “Stay with us, for it is nearly evening and the day is almost over.” So He went in to stay with them.
bsb.24:30: While He was reclining at the table with them, He took bread, spoke a blessing and broke it, and gave it to them.
bsb.24:31: Then their eyes were opened and they recognized Jesus—and He disappeared from their sight.
bsb.24:32: They asked each other, “Were not our hearts burning within us as He spoke with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?”
bsb.24:33: And they got up that very hour and returned to Jerusalem. There they found the Eleven and those with them, gathered together
bsb.24:34: and saying, “The Lord has indeed risen and has appeared to Simon!”
bsb.24:35: Then the two told what had happened on the road, and how they had recognized Jesus in the breaking of the bread.
bsb.24:36: While they were describing these events, Jesus Himself stood among them and said, “Peace be with you.”
bsb.24:37: But they were startled and frightened, thinking they had seen a spirit.
bsb.24:38: “Why are you troubled,” Jesus asked, “and why do doubts arise in your hearts?
bsb.24:39: Look at My hands and My feet. It is I Myself. Touch Me and see—for a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see I have.”
bsb.24:40: And when He had said this, He showed them His hands and feet.
bsb.24:41: While they were still in disbelief because of their joy and amazement, He asked them, “Do you have anything here to eat?”
bsb.24:42: So they gave Him a piece of broiled fish,
bsb.24:43: and He took it and ate it in front of them.
bsb.24:44: Jesus said to them, “These are the words I spoke to you while I was still with you: Everything must be fulfilled that is written about Me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms.”
bsb.24:45: Then He opened their minds to understand the Scriptures.
bsb.24:46: And He told them, “This is what is written: The Christ will suffer and rise from the dead on the third day,
bsb.24:47: and in His name repentance and forgiveness of sins will be proclaimed to all nations, beginning in Jerusalem.
bsb.24:48: You are witnesses of these things.
bsb.24:49: And behold, I am sending the promise of My Father upon you. But remain in the city until you have been clothed with power from on high.”
bsb.24:50: When Jesus had led them out as far as Bethany, He lifted up His hands and blessed them.
bsb.24:51: While He was blessing them, He left them and was carried up into heaven.
bsb.24:52: And they worshiped Him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy,
bsb.24:53: praising God continually in the temple.

asv.1:1: Forasmuch as many have taken in hand to draw up a narrative concerning those matters which have been fulfilled among us,
asv.1:2: even as they delivered them unto us, who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and ministers of the word,
asv.1:3: it seemed good to me also, having traced the course of all things accurately from the first, to write unto thee in order, most excellent Theophilus;
asv.1:4: that thou mightest know the certainty concerning the things wherein thou wast instructed.
asv.1:5: There was in the days of Herod, king of Judæa, a certain priest named Zacharias, of the course of Abijah: and he had a wife of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elisabeth.
asv.1:6: And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.
asv.1:7: And they had no child, because that Elisabeth was barren, and they both were now well stricken in years.
asv.1:8: Now it came to pass, while he executed the priest’s office before God in the order of his course,
asv.1:9: according to the custom of the priest’s office, his lot was to enter into the temple of the Lord and burn incense.
asv.1:10: And the whole multitude of the people were praying without at the hour of incense.
asv.1:11: And there appeared unto him an angel of the Lord standing on the right side of the altar of incense.
asv.1:12: And Zacharias was troubled when he saw him, and fear fell upon him.
asv.1:13: But the angel said unto him, Fear not, Zacharias: because thy supplication is heard, and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John.
asv.1:14: And thou shalt have joy and gladness; and many shall rejoice at his birth.
asv.1:15: For he shall be great in the sight of the Lord, and he shall drink no wine nor strong drink; and he shall be filled with the Holy Spirit, even from his mother’s womb.
asv.1:16: And many of the children of Israel shall he turn unto the Lord their God.
asv.1:17: And he shall go before his face in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the disobedient to walk in the wisdom of the just; to make ready for the Lord a people prepared for him.
asv.1:18: And Zacharias said unto the angel, Whereby shall I know this? for I am an old man, and my wife well stricken in years.
asv.1:19: And the angel answering said unto him, I am Gabriel, that stand in the presence of God; and I was sent to speak unto thee, and to bring thee these good tidings.
asv.1:20: And behold, thou shalt be silent and not able to speak, until the day that these things shall come to pass, because thou believedst not my words, which shall be fulfilled in their season.
asv.1:21: And the people were waiting for Zacharias, and they marvelled while he tarried in the temple.
asv.1:22: And when he came out, he could not speak unto them: and they perceived that he had seen a vision in the temple: and he continued making signs unto them, and remained dumb.
asv.1:23: And it came to pass, when the days of his ministration were fulfilled, he departed unto his house.
asv.1:24: And after these days Elisabeth his wife conceived; and she hid herself five months, saying,
asv.1:25: Thus hath the Lord done unto me in the days wherein he looked upon me, to take away my reproach among men.
asv.1:26: Now in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God unto a city of Galilee, named Nazareth,
asv.1:27: to a virgin betrothed to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin’s name was Mary.
asv.1:28: And he came in unto her, and said, Hail, thou that art highly favored, the Lord is with thee.
asv.1:29: But she was greatly troubled at the saying, and cast in her mind what manner of salutation this might be.
asv.1:30: And the angel said unto her, Fear not, Mary: for thou hast found favor with God.
asv.1:31: And behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS.
asv.1:32: He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Most High: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David:
asv.1:33: and he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever; and of his kingdom there shall be no end.
asv.1:34: And Mary said unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?
asv.1:35: And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Spirit shall come upon thee, and the power of the Most High shall overshadow thee: wherefore also the holy thing which is begotten shall be called the Son of God.
asv.1:36: And behold, Elisabeth thy kinswoman, she also hath conceived a son in her old age; and this is the sixth month with her that was called barren.
asv.1:37: For no word from God shall be void of power.
asv.1:38: And Mary said, Behold, the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word. And the angel departed from her.
asv.1:39: And Mary arose in these days and went into the hill country with haste, into a city of Judah;
asv.1:40: and entered into the house of Zacharias and saluted Elisabeth.
asv.1:41: And it came to pass, when Elisabeth heard the salutation of Mary, the babe leaped in her womb; and Elisabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit;
asv.1:42: and she lifted up her voice with a loud cry, and said, Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.
asv.1:43: And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come unto me?
asv.1:44: For behold, when the voice of thy salutation came into mine ears, the babe leaped in my womb for joy.
asv.1:45: And blessed is she that believed; for there shall be a fulfilment of the things which have been spoken to her from the Lord.
asv.1:46: And Mary said, My soul doth magnify the Lord,
asv.1:47: And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour.
asv.1:48: For he hath looked upon the low estate of his handmaid: For behold, from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed.
asv.1:49: For he that is mighty hath done to me great things; And holy is his name.
asv.1:50: And his mercy is unto generations and generations On them that fear him.
asv.1:51: He hath showed strength with his arm; He hath scattered the proud in the imagination of their heart.
asv.1:52: He hath put down princes from their thrones, And hath exalted them of low degree.
asv.1:53: The hungry he hath filled with good things; And the rich he hath sent empty away.
asv.1:54: He hath given help to Israel his servant, That he might remember mercy
asv.1:55: (As he spake unto our fathers) Toward Abraham and his seed for ever.
asv.1:56: And Mary abode with her about three months, and returned unto her house.
asv.1:57: Now Elisabeth’s time was fulfilled that she should be delivered; and she brought forth a son.
asv.1:58: And her neighbors and her kinsfolk heard that the Lord had magnified his mercy towards her; and they rejoiced with her.
asv.1:59: And it came to pass on the eighth day, that they came to circumcise the child; and they would have called him Zacharias, after the name of his father.
asv.1:60: And his mother answered and said, Not so; but he shall be called John.
asv.1:61: And they said unto her, There is none of thy kindred that is called by this name.
asv.1:62: And they made signs to his father, what he would have him called.
asv.1:63: And he asked for a writing tablet, and wrote, saying, His name is John. And they marvelled all.
asv.1:64: And his mouth was opened immediately, and his tongue loosed, and he spake, blessing God.
asv.1:65: And fear came on all that dwelt round about them: and all these sayings were noised abroad throughout all the hill country of Judæa.
asv.1:66: And all that heard them laid them up in their heart, saying, What then shall this child be? For the hand of the Lord was with him.
asv.1:67: And his father Zacharias was filled with the Holy Spirit, and prophesied, saying,
asv.1:68: Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel; For he hath visited and wrought redemption for his people,
asv.1:69: And hath raised up a horn of salvation for us In the house of his servant David
asv.1:70: (As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets that have been from of old),
asv.1:71: Salvation from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us;
asv.1:72: To show mercy towards our fathers, And to remember his holy covenant;
asv.1:73: The oath which he sware unto Abraham our father,
asv.1:74: To grant unto us that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies Should serve him without fear,
asv.1:75: In holiness and righteousness before him all our days.
asv.1:76: Yea and thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Most High: For thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to make ready his ways;
asv.1:77: To give knowledge of salvation unto his people In the remission of their sins,
asv.1:78: Because of the tender mercy of our God, Whereby the dayspring from on high shall visit us,
asv.1:79: To shine upon them that sit in darkness and the shadow of death; To guide our feet into the way of peace.
asv.1:80: And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, and was in the deserts till the day of his showing unto Israel.
asv.2:1: Now it came to pass in those days, there went out a decree from Cæsar Augustus, that all the world should be enrolled.
asv.2:2: This was the first enrolment made when Quirinius was governor of Syria.
asv.2:3: And all went to enrol themselves, every one to his own city.
asv.2:4: And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judæa, to the city of David, which is called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and family of David;
asv.2:5: to enrol himself with Mary, who was betrothed to him, being great with child.
asv.2:6: And it came to pass, while they were there, the days were fulfilled that she should be delivered.
asv.2:7: And she brought forth her firstborn son; and she wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the inn.
asv.2:8: And there were shepherds in the same country abiding in the field, and keeping watch by night over their flock.
asv.2:9: And an angel of the Lord stood by them, and the glory of the Lord shone round about them: and they were sore afraid.
asv.2:10: And the angel said unto them, Be not afraid; for behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy which shall be to all the people:
asv.2:11: for there is born to you this day in the city of David a Saviour, who is Christ the Lord.
asv.2:12: And this is the sign unto you: Ye shall find a babe wrapped in swaddling clothes, and lying in a manger.
asv.2:13: And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host praising God, and saying,
asv.2:14: Glory to God in the highest, And on earth peace among men in whom he is well pleased.
asv.2:15: And it came to pass, when the angels went away from them into heaven, the shepherds said one to another, Let us now go even unto Bethlehem, and see this thing that is come to pass, which the Lord hath made known unto us.
asv.2:16: And they came with haste, and found both Mary and Joseph, and the babe lying in the manger.
asv.2:17: And when they saw it, they made known concerning the saying which was spoken to them about this child.
asv.2:18: And all that heard it wondered at the things which were spoken unto them by the shepherds.
asv.2:19: But Mary kept all these sayings, pondering them in her heart.
asv.2:20: And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things that they had heard and seen, even as it was spoken unto them.
asv.2:21: And when eight days were fulfilled for circumcising him, his name was called JESUS, which was so called by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
asv.2:22: And when the days of their purification according to the law of Moses were fulfilled, they brought him up to Jerusalem, to present him to the Lord
asv.2:23: (as it is written in the law of the Lord, Every male that openeth the womb shall be called holy to the Lord),
asv.2:24: and to offer a sacrifice according to that which is said in the law of the Lord, A pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons.
asv.2:25: And behold, there was a man in Jerusalem, whose name was Simeon; and this man was righteous and devout, looking for the consolation of Israel: and the Holy Spirit was upon him.
asv.2:26: And it had been revealed unto him by the Holy Spirit, that he should not see death, before he had seen the Lord’s Christ.
asv.2:27: And he came in the Spirit into the temple: and when the parents brought in the child Jesus, that they might do concerning him after the custom of the law,
asv.2:28: then he received him into his arms, and blessed God, and said,
asv.2:29: Now lettest thou thy servant depart, Lord, According to thy word, in peace;
asv.2:30: For mine eyes have seen thy salvation,
asv.2:31: Which thou hast prepared before the face of all peoples;
asv.2:32: A light for revelation to the Gentiles, And the glory of thy people Israel.
asv.2:33: And his father and his mother were marvelling at the things which were spoken concerning him;
asv.2:34: and Simeon blessed them, and said unto Mary his mother, Behold, this child is set for the falling and the rising of many in Israel; and for a sign which is spoken against;
asv.2:35: yea and a sword shall pierce through thine own soul; that thoughts out of many hearts may be revealed.
asv.2:36: And there was one Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher (she was of a great age, having lived with a husband seven years from her virginity,
asv.2:37: and she had been a widow even unto fourscore and four years), who departed not from the temple, worshipping with fastings and supplications night and day.
asv.2:38: And coming up at that very hour she gave thanks unto God, and spake of him to all them that were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem.
asv.2:39: And when they had accomplished all things that were according to the law of the Lord, they returned into Galilee, to their own city Nazareth.
asv.2:40: And the child grew, and waxed strong, filled with wisdom: and the grace of God was upon him.
asv.2:41: And his parents went every year to Jerusalem at the feast of the passover.
asv.2:42: And when he was twelve years old, they went up after the custom of the feast;
asv.2:43: and when they had fulfilled the days, as they were returning, the boy Jesus tarried behind in Jerusalem; and his parents knew it not;
asv.2:44: but supposing him to be in the company, they went a day’s journey; and they sought for him among their kinsfolk and acquaintance:
asv.2:45: and when they found him not, they returned to Jerusalem, seeking for him.
asv.2:46: And it came to pass, after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the teachers, both hearing them, and asking them questions:
asv.2:47: and all that heard him were amazed at his understanding and his answers.
asv.2:48: And when they saw him, they were astonished; and his mother said unto him, Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I sought thee sorrowing.
asv.2:49: And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? knew ye not that I must be in my Father’s house?
asv.2:50: And they understood not the saying which he spake unto them.
asv.2:51: And he went down with them, and came to Nazareth; and he was subject unto them: and his mother kept all these sayings in her heart.
asv.2:52: And Jesus advanced in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and men.
asv.3:1: Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Cæsar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judæa, and Herod being tetrarch of Galilee, and his brother Philip tetrarch of the region of Ituræa and Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene,
asv.3:2: in the high-priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came unto John the son of Zacharias in the wilderness.
asv.3:3: And he came into all the region round about the Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance unto remission of sins;
asv.3:4: as it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make ye ready the way of the Lord, Make his paths straight.
asv.3:5: Every valley shall be filled, And every mountain and hill shall be brought low; And the crooked shall become straight, And the rough ways smooth;
asv.3:6: And all flesh shall see the salvation of God.
asv.3:7: He said therefore to the multitudes that went out to be baptized of him, Ye offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?
asv.3:8: Bring forth therefore fruits worthy of repentance, and begin not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.
asv.3:9: And even now the axe also lieth at the root of the trees: every tree therefore that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.
asv.3:10: And the multitudes asked him, saying, What then must we do?
asv.3:11: And he answered and said unto them, He that hath two coats, let him impart to him that hath none; and he that hath food, let him do likewise.
asv.3:12: And there came also publicans to be baptized, and they said unto him, Teacher, what must we do?
asv.3:13: And he said unto them, Extort no more than that which is appointed you.
asv.3:14: And soldiers also asked him, saying, And we, what must we do? And he said unto them, Extort from no man by violence, neither accuse any one wrongfully; and be content with your wages.
asv.3:15: And as the people were in expectation, and all men reasoned in their hearts concerning John, whether haply he were the Christ;
asv.3:16: John answered, saying unto them all, I indeed baptize you with water; but there cometh he that is mightier than I, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to unloose: he shall baptize you in the Holy Spirit and in fire:
asv.3:17: whose fan is in his hand, thoroughly to cleanse his threshing-floor, and to gather the wheat into his garner; but the chaff he will burn up with unquenchable fire.
asv.3:18: With many other exhortations therefore preached he good tidings unto the people;
asv.3:19: but Herod the tetrarch, being reproved by him for Herodias his brother’s wife, and for all the evil things which Herod had done,
asv.3:20: added this also to them all, that he shut up John in prison.
asv.3:21: Now it came to pass, when all the people were baptized, that, Jesus also having been baptized, and praying, the heaven was opened,
asv.3:22: and the Holy Spirit descended in a bodily form, as a dove, upon him, and a voice came out of heaven, Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased.
asv.3:23: And Jesus himself, when he began to teach, was about thirty years of age, being the son (as was supposed) of Joseph, the son of Heli,
asv.3:24: the son of Matthat, the son of Levi, the son of Melchi, the son of Jannai, the son of Joseph,
asv.3:25: the son of Mattathias, the son of Amos, the son of Nahum, the son of Esli, the son of Naggai,
asv.3:26: the son of Maath, the son of Mattathias, the son of Semein, the son of Josech, the son of Joda,
asv.3:27: the son of Joanan, the son of Rhesa, the son of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, the son of Neri,
asv.3:28: the son of Melchi, the son of Addi, the son of Cosam, the son of Elmadam, the son of Er,
asv.3:29: the son of Jesus, the son of Eliezer, the son of Jorim, the son of Matthat, the son of Levi,
asv.3:30: the son of Symeon, the son of Judas, the son of Joseph, the son of Jonam, the son of Eliakim,
asv.3:31: the son of Melea, the son of Menna, the son of Mattatha, the son of Nathan, the son of David,
asv.3:32: the son of Jesse, the son of Obed, the son of Boaz, the son of Salmon, the son of Nahshon,
asv.3:33: the son of Amminadab, the son of Arni, the son of Hezron, the son of Perez, the son of Judah,
asv.3:34: the son of Jacob, the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham, the son of Terah, the son of Nahor,
asv.3:35: the son of Serug, the son of Reu, the son of Peleg, the son of Eber, the son of Shelah,
asv.3:36: the son of Cainan, the son of Arphaxad, the son of Shem, the son of Noah, the son of Lamech,
asv.3:37: the son of Methuselah, the son of Enoch, the son of Jared, the son of Mahalaleel, the son of Cainan,
asv.3:38: the son of Enos, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, the son of God.
asv.4:1: And Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan, and was led in the Spirit in the wilderness
asv.4:2: during forty days, being tempted of the devil. And he did eat nothing in those days: and when they were completed, he hungered.
asv.4:3: And the devil said unto him, If thou art the Son of God, command this stone that it become bread.
asv.4:4: And Jesus answered unto him, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone.
asv.4:5: And he led him up, and showed him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.
asv.4:6: And the devil said unto him, To thee will I give all this authority, and the glory of them: for it hath been delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.
asv.4:7: If thou therefore wilt worship before me, it shall all be thine.
asv.4:8: And Jesus answered and said unto him, It is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.
asv.4:9: And he led him to Jerusalem, and set him on the pinnacle of the temple, and said unto him, If thou art the Son of God, cast thyself down from hence:
asv.4:10: for it is written, He shall give his angels charge concerning thee, to guard thee:
asv.4:11: and, On their hands they shall bear thee up, Lest haply thou dash thy foot against a stone.
asv.4:12: And Jesus answering said unto him, It is said, Thou shalt not make trial of the Lord thy God.
asv.4:13: And when the devil had completed every temptation, he departed from him for a season.
asv.4:14: And Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit into Galilee: and a fame went out concerning him through all the region round about.
asv.4:15: And he taught in their synagogues, being glorified of all.
asv.4:16: And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up: and he entered, as his custom was, into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up to read.
asv.4:17: And there was delivered unto him the book of the prophet Isaiah. And he opened the book, and found the place where it was written,
asv.4:18: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, Because he anointed me to preach good tidings to the poor: He hath sent me to proclaim release to the captives, And recovering of sight to the blind, To set at liberty them that are bruised,
asv.4:19: To proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord.
asv.4:20: And he closed the book, and gave it back to the attendant, and sat down: and the eyes of all in the synagogue were fastened on him.
asv.4:21: And he began to say unto them, To-day hath this scripture been fulfilled in your ears.
asv.4:22: And all bare him witness, and wondered at the words of grace which proceeded out of his mouth: and they said, Is not this Joseph’s son?
asv.4:23: And he said unto them, Doubtless ye will say unto me this parable, Physician, heal thyself: whatsoever we have heard done at Capernaum, do also here in thine own country.
asv.4:24: And he said, Verily I say unto you, No prophet is acceptable in his own country.
asv.4:25: But of a truth I say unto you, There were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, when there came a great famine over all the land;
asv.4:26: and unto none of them was Elijah sent, but only to Zarephath, in the land of Sidon, unto a woman that was a widow.
asv.4:27: And there were many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, but only Naaman the Syrian.
asv.4:28: And they were all filled with wrath in the synagogue, as they heard these things;
asv.4:29: and they rose up, and cast him forth out of the city, and led him unto the brow of the hill whereon their city was built, that they might throw him down headlong.
asv.4:30: But he passing through the midst of them went his way.
asv.4:31: And he came down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee. And he was teaching them on the sabbath day:
asv.4:32: and they were astonished at his teaching; for his word was with authority.
asv.4:33: And in the synagogue there was a man, that had a spirit of an unclean demon; and he cried out with a loud voice,
asv.4:34: Ah! what have we to do with thee, Jesus thou Nazarene? art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art, the Holy One of God.
asv.4:35: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace, and come out of him. And when the demon had thrown him down in the midst, he came out of him, having done him no hurt.
asv.4:36: And amazement came upon all, and they spake together, one with another, saying, What is this word? for with authority and power he commandeth the unclean spirits, and they come out.
asv.4:37: And there went forth a rumor concerning him into every place of the region round about.
asv.4:38: And he rose up from the synagogue, and entered into the house of Simon. And Simon’s wife’s mother was holden with a great fever; and they besought him for her.
asv.4:39: And he stood over her, and rebuked the fever; and it left her: and immediately she rose up and ministered unto them.
asv.4:40: And when the sun was setting, all they that had any sick with divers diseases brought them unto him; and he laid his hands on every one of them, and healed them.
asv.4:41: And demons also came out from many, crying out, and saying, Thou art the Son of God. And rebuking them, he suffered them not to speak, because they knew that he was the Christ.
asv.4:42: And when it was day, he came out and went into a desert place: and the multitudes sought after him, and came unto him, and would have stayed him, that he should not go from them.
asv.4:43: But he said unto them, I must preach the good tidings of the kingdom of God to the other cities also: for therefore was I sent.
asv.4:44: And he was preaching in the synagogues of Galilee.
asv.5:1: Now it came to pass, while the multitude pressed upon him and heard the word of God, that he was standing by the lake of Gennesaret;
asv.5:2: and he saw two boats standing by the lake: but the fishermen had gone out of them, and were washing their nets.
asv.5:3: And he entered into one of the boats, which was Simon’s, and asked him to put out a little from the land. And he sat down and taught the multitudes out of the boat.
asv.5:4: And when he had left speaking, he said unto Simon, Put out into the deep, and let down your nets for a draught.
asv.5:5: And Simon answered and said, Master, we toiled all night, and took nothing: but at thy word I will let down the nets.
asv.5:6: And when they had done this, they inclosed a great multitude of fishes; and their nets were breaking;
asv.5:7: and they beckoned unto their partners in the other boat, that they should come and help them. And they came, and filled both the boats, so that they began to sink.
asv.5:8: But Simon Peter, when he saw it, fell down at Jesus’ knees, saying, Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord.
asv.5:9: For he was amazed, and all that were with him, at the draught of the fishes which they had taken;
asv.5:10: and so were also James and John, sons of Zebedee, who were partners with Simon. And Jesus said unto Simon, Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men.
asv.5:11: And when they had brought their boats to land, they left all, and followed him.
asv.5:12: And it came to pass, while he was in one of the cities, behold, a man full of leprosy: and when he saw Jesus, he fell on his face, and besought him, saying, Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
asv.5:13: And he stretched forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will; be thou made clean. And straightway the leprosy departed from him.
asv.5:14: And he charged him to tell no man: but go thy way, and show thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing, according as Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.
asv.5:15: But so much the more went abroad the report concerning him: and great multitudes came together to hear, and to be healed of their infirmities.
asv.5:16: But he withdrew himself in the deserts, and prayed.
asv.5:17: And it came to pass on one of those days, that he was teaching; and there were Pharisees and doctors of the law sitting by, who were come out of every village of Galilee and Judæa and Jerusalem: and the power of the Lord was with him to heal.
asv.5:18: And behold, men bring on a bed a man that was palsied: and they sought to bring him in, and to lay him before him.
asv.5:19: And not finding by what way they might bring him in because of the multitude, they went up to the housetop, and let him down through the tiles with his couch into the midst before Jesus.
asv.5:20: And seeing their faith, he said, Man, thy sins are forgiven thee.
asv.5:21: And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, Who is this that speaketh blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone?
asv.5:22: But Jesus perceiving their reasonings, answered and said unto them, Why reason ye in your hearts?
asv.5:23: Which is easier, to say, Thy sins are forgiven thee; or to say, Arise and walk?
asv.5:24: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath authority on earth to forgive sins (he said unto him that was palsied), I say unto thee, Arise, and take up thy couch, and go unto thy house.
asv.5:25: And immediately he rose up before them, and took up that whereon he lay, and departed to his house, glorifying God.
asv.5:26: And amazement took hold on all, and they glorified God; and they were filled with fear, saying, We have seen strange things to-day.
asv.5:27: And after these things he went forth, and beheld a publican, named Levi, sitting at the place of toll, and said unto him, Follow me.
asv.5:28: And he forsook all, and rose up and followed him.
asv.5:29: And Levi made him a great feast in his house: and there was a great multitude of publicans and of others that were sitting at meat with them.
asv.5:30: And the Pharisees and their scribes murmured against his disciples, saying, Why do ye eat and drink with the publicans and sinners?
asv.5:31: And Jesus answering said unto them, They that are in health have no need of a physician; but they that are sick.
asv.5:32: I am not come to call the righteous but sinners to repentance.
asv.5:33: And they said unto him, The disciples of John fast often, and make supplications; likewise also the disciples of the Pharisees; but thine eat and drink.
asv.5:34: And Jesus said unto them, Can ye make the sons of the bride-chamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them?
asv.5:35: But the days will come; and when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, then will they fast in those days.
asv.5:36: And he spake also a parable unto them: No man rendeth a piece from a new garment and putteth it upon an old garment; else he will rend the new, and also the piece from the new will not agree with the old.
asv.5:37: And no man putteth new wine into old wine-skins; else the new wine will burst the skins, and itself will be spilled, and the skins will perish.
asv.5:38: But new wine must be put into fresh wine-skins.
asv.5:39: And no man having drunk old wine desireth new; for he saith, The old is good.
asv.6:1: Now it came to pass on a sabbath, that he was going through the grainfields; and his disciples plucked the ears, and did eat, rubbing them in their hands.
asv.6:2: But certain of the Pharisees said, Why do ye that which it is not lawful to do on the sabbath day?
asv.6:3: And Jesus answering them said, Have ye not read even this, what David did, when he was hungry, he, and they that were with him;
asv.6:4: how he entered into the house of God, and took and ate the showbread, and gave also to them that were with him; which it is not lawful to eat save for the priests alone?
asv.6:5: And he said unto them, The Son of man is lord of the sabbath.
asv.6:6: And it came to pass on another sabbath, that he entered into the synagogue and taught: and there was a man there, and his right hand was withered.
asv.6:7: And the scribes and the Pharisees watched him, whether he would heal on the sabbath; that they might find how to accuse him.
asv.6:8: But he knew their thoughts; and he said to the man that had his hand withered, Rise up, and stand forth in the midst. And he arose and stood forth.
asv.6:9: And Jesus said unto them, I ask you, Is it lawful on the sabbath to do good, or to do harm? to save a life, or to destroy it?
asv.6:10: And he looked round about on them all, and said unto him, Stretch forth thy hand. And he did so: and his hand was restored.
asv.6:11: But they were filled with madness; and communed one with another what they might do to Jesus.
asv.6:12: And it came to pass in these days, that he went out into the mountain to pray; and he continued all night in prayer to God.
asv.6:13: And when it was day, he called his disciples; and he chose from them twelve, whom also he named apostles:
asv.6:14: Simon, whom he also named Peter, and Andrew his brother, and James and John, and Philip and Bartholomew,
asv.6:15: and Matthew and Thomas, and James the son of Alphæus, and Simon who was called the Zealot,
asv.6:16: and Judas the son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor;
asv.6:17: and he came down with them, and stood on a level place, and a great multitude of his disciples, and a great number of the people from all Judæa and Jerusalem, and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon, who came to hear him, and to be healed of their diseases;
asv.6:18: and they that were troubled with unclean spirits were healed.
asv.6:19: And all the multitude sought to touch him; for power came forth from him, and healed them all.
asv.6:20: And he lifted up his eyes on his disciples, and said, Blessed are ye poor: for yours is the kingdom of God.
asv.6:21: Blessed are ye that hunger now: for ye shall be filled. Blessed are ye that weep now: for ye shall laugh.
asv.6:22: Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company, and reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man’s sake.
asv.6:23: Rejoice in that day, and leap for joy: for behold, your reward is great in heaven; for in the same manner did their fathers unto the prophets.
asv.6:24: But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation.
asv.6:25: Woe unto you, ye that are full now! for ye shall hunger. Woe unto you, ye that laugh now! for ye shall mourn and weep.
asv.6:26: Woe unto you, when all men shall speak well of you! for in the same manner did their fathers to the false prophets.
asv.6:27: But I say unto you that hear, Love your enemies, do good to them that hate you,
asv.6:28: bless them that curse you, pray for them that despitefully use you.
asv.6:29: To him that smiteth thee on the one cheek offer also the other; and from him that taketh away thy cloak withhold not thy coat also.
asv.6:30: Give to every one that asketh thee; and of him that taketh away thy goods ask them not again.
asv.6:31: And as ye would that men should do to you, do ye also to them likewise.
